usage: agenterm-cu --target <current|ssh|vnc|rdp> [--grant observe,actuate] <command> [args...]
       agenterm-cu --ssh <user@host> [--ssh-port N] [--ssh-identity PATH] [--ssh-cu PATH]
                   [--ssh-env KEY=VAL]... [--grant observe,actuate] <command> [args...]
       agenterm-cu --vnc <host[:port]> [--vnc-port N] [--vnc-cu PATH]
                   [--vnc-env KEY=VAL]... [--grant observe,actuate] <command> [args...]
       agenterm-cu --rdp <host[:port]> [--grant observe,actuate] <command> [args...]
       agenterm-cu exec [--grant observe,actuate] --json '<command-json>' | --json -
       agenterm-cu grant create|list|revoke ...     bounded persisted grants (help grant)
       agenterm-cu host | hotkeys                   desktop menu and global shortcuts
       agenterm-cu help <verb> | <verb> --help      one verb's full reference
       agenterm-cu verbs [--json]                   the verb table (JSON when piped)

Global flags:
  --target current|ssh|vnc|rdp  explicit target reference (required unless --ssh/--vnc/--rdp)
  --ssh <user@host>         ssh target destination (implies --target ssh; or AGENTERM_CU_SSH)
  --ssh-port N              OpenSSH -p (or AGENTERM_CU_SSH_PORT)
  --ssh-identity PATH       OpenSSH -i (or AGENTERM_CU_SSH_IDENTITY)
  --ssh-cu PATH             remote agenterm-cu path (or AGENTERM_CU_SSH_CU; default: this exe)
  --ssh-env KEY=VAL         remote env for the worker (repeatable; also AGENTERM_CU_SSH_ENV)
  --vnc <host[:port]>       vnc/RFB endpoint (implies --target vnc; or AGENTERM_CU_VNC)
  --vnc-port N              RFB TCP port when --vnc omits :port (or AGENTERM_CU_VNC_PORT; default 5900)
  --vnc-cu PATH             session worker agenterm-cu path (or AGENTERM_CU_VNC_CU; default: this exe)
  --vnc-env KEY=VAL         session env for the worker (repeatable; also AGENTERM_CU_VNC_ENV)
  --rdp <host[:port]>       rdp endpoint syntax only (implies --target rdp; PLACEHOLDER --
                            no connect / TLS / CredSSP; always rdp_unavailable)
  --grant observe,actuate   strict authorization scopes; CLI wins over
                            AGENTERM_CU_GRANT and sources never union
  --grant-id ID             bounded persisted current-target grant selector;
                            mutually exclusive with every other auth source
  --grant-store PATH        explicit store override; valid only with --grant-id
  --request-id ID           stable at-most-once identity for one mutating command
  --session ID              active runtime session owning the request identity
  --session-lease LEASE     bearer lease for --session; never persisted or audited
                            all three fields are required; SSH/VNC admit them at the effect worker

Transports: ssh and vnc run the same verbs on an agenterm-cu --target current
  worker (OpenSSH stdio / the shared RFB session); rdp parses, authorizes and
  fails closed with rdp_unavailable. `help ssh|vnc|rdp` carry the evidence notes.

Commands  (scope = required --grant; `help <verb>` prints arguments and behaviour)

System & permissions
  capabilities (caps)               observe  per-target capability matrix for this host
  permissions                       observe  permission state, affected verbs and repair guidance
  doctor                            observe  bounded host, permission and desktop-bridge health report

Windows & apps
  windows (focused-window)          observe  top-level window inventory, filtered and paged
  windows-watch                     observe  poll-diff over the window inventory
  apps                              observe  running apps from top-level windows; --all adds installed
  app (launch, quit, hide, show)    actuate  hide / show / quit / launch a whole application
  unlock                            observe  ask the app to build its full a11y tree
  close                             actuate  close one window through its own close control (gated)
  activate                          actuate  make one exact window the desktop foreground owner
  raise                             actuate  lift one window inside its own app's z-order
  minimize                          actuate  minimize one window through its own affordance (gated)
  restore                           actuate  un-minimize one window without activating its app (gated)
  receipts                          observe  read the target's crash-persistent receipt file
  spaces                            observe  macOS managed Space inventory (read-only)
  displays                          observe  native screen frames

Processes
  ps                                observe  bounded process inventory from the shared platform facade
  process-state (process state)     observe  observe one pid with a stable process-start identity
  process-usage (process usage)     observe  sample or watch identity-bound CPU, memory and page faults
  process-wait (process wait)       observe  wait for one identity-bound process instance to exit
  process-kill (process kill, kill) actuate  terminate one exact identity-bound process object
  process-watch (process watch)     observe  watch a bounded, identity-safe process-set diff
shell-exec                        actuate  run one bounded contained host-shell command

Network
  network-interfaces (network interfaces) observe  bounded native interface inventory
  network-probe (network probe)     observe  resolve once and measure bounded TCP reachability

AgenTerm terminals
  terminal-list (terminal list)     observe  list AgenTerm-owned tabs with epoch-scoped stable ids
  terminal-read (terminal read)     observe  read one bounded current-screen snapshot
  terminal-send (terminal send)     actuate  send exact UTF-8 bytes to one AgenTerm-owned tab
  terminal-wait (terminal wait)     observe  wait for screen text, process exit, or fully drained exit

Accessibility: observe
  tree (elements)                   observe  bounded a11y tree of a window; --flat numbers nodes
  query (inspect, find, read)       observe  bounded, filtered flat node list
  hit                               observe  the a11y node under a screen point
  focused                           observe  the app's own focused control inside the window
  observe                           observe  bounded a11y event stream by poll-diff
  snapshot                          observe  name a bounded tree as a baseline for diff
  diff                              observe  what changed since a snapshot baseline
  verify                            observe  one tree read checked against --expect items
  menu-inspect (menu inspect)       observe  read the menu bar in the background
  get-text                          observe  independent AT-SPI Text.GetText on a named / focused node
  get-extents                       observe  independent AT-SPI Component.GetExtents(Screen)
  get-selection                     observe  independent AT-SPI Text selection read-back
  get-caret                         observe  independent AT-SPI caret offset read-back
  wait                              observe  poll until a window / node / text condition holds
  screenshot (shot)                 observe  capture a window or the screen to a PNG file
  zoom                              observe  crop one region of a window capture to a PNG
  pointer-position (cursor)         observe  absolute pointer coordinates, no event injected

Accessibility: actuate
  invoke                            actuate  one semantic a11y action on one node
  menu-invoke (menu invoke)         actuate  press one menu item by exact path in the background
  click (dclick, rclick)            actuate  click a node by --node / --name, or --coords --degraded
  drag                              actuate  press, move, release as one gesture (--degraded)
  focus                             actuate  focus a node by --node or --window --name
  send-text (type)                  actuate  write text into a named / focused node, or type into focus
  send-keys (key)                   actuate  deliver key chords to a named / focused node, or the focus
  scroll                            actuate  AT-SPI Component.ScrollTo(TopEdge) on a named node
  select                            actuate  AT-SPI Text.SetSelection on a named node
  set-caret                         actuate  AT-SPI Text.SetCaretOffset on a named node
  pointer-move (move)               actuate  move the pointer to absolute screen coordinates

Browser page & tabs
  page-js (page read)               observe  CDP Runtime.evaluate against one page target
  page-targets (page targets)       observe  the CDP /json target inventory
  page-text (page text)             observe  visible page text in reading order (a11y tree or CDP)
  page-find (page find)             observe  nodes of one CDP page target by CSS, text or role
  page-click (page click)           actuate  click one node or point in a CDP page target
  page-download (page download)     actuate  click and verify one background CDP download on disk
  page-hover (page hover)           actuate  hover one viewport point of a CDP page target in place
  page-scroll (page scroll)         actuate  wheel one viewport point of a CDP page target in place
  page-files (page files)           actuate  set and verify one CDP file input without a picker
  page-drag (page drag)             actuate  drag between two viewport points of a CDP target in place
  page-dialog (page dialog)         actuate  accept or dismiss one real JavaScript dialog on a CDP target
  page-fill (page fill)             actuate  type into one field of a CDP page target in place
  page-type (page type)             actuate  insert text at a CDP page target's current focus
  page-nav (page nav)               actuate  navigate one CDP page target without selecting it
  page-screenshot (page screenshot) observe  PNG of one CDP page target (background may refuse)
  tab-list (tab list)               observe  the browser tab strip through the a11y tree
  tab-select (tab select)           actuate  select one tab in the background
  tab-close (tab close)             actuate  close one tab through its own close button or CDP (gated)
  browser-profiles (browser profiles) observe  running Chromium profiles and windows
  browser-open (browser open)       actuate  open one profile's window / URL in the running browser
  page                              observe  MCU page group; unmapped page verbs answer typed

Clipboard
  clipboard-read (clip, clipboard)    observe  clipboard text or bounded native bytes
  clipboard-write (clipboard write) actuate  publish one native type from a regular file
  clipboard-write-file (clipboard write-file)
                                    actuate  put a file reference on the clipboard
  clipboard-clear (clipboard clear) actuate  empty the clipboard (planned unless --apply)
  copy                              actuate  copy a node's AT-SPI text onto the native clipboard
  paste                             actuate  write clipboard text into a node via AT-SPI

Window placement
  window-place                      actuate  one of the 18 placement actions on a window
  frame                             actuate  window-place --action frame
  movewin                           actuate  window-place move (keeps the current size)
  resize                            actuate  window-place resize (keeps the current origin)
  maximize                          actuate  window-place --action fullscreen
  orderwin                          actuate  relative z-order: raise --window above / below --relative

Transports
  exec                              none     run one JSON command (the ssh / vnc worker mode)

Grants, host & help
  grant                             none     create / list / revoke bounded persisted grants
  host (hotkeys)                    none     resident desktop menu and global shortcuts
  help                              none     this list, or one verb's full reference
  verbs                             none     the verb table (JSON when piped, or --json / --text)

MCU-aligned verbs with no mechanism here (pty, simulator, drag, ...) answer typed
unsupported, never unknown; `capabilities` lists them per target.
All replies are JSON on stdout: {"ok":bool,"target":..,"command":..,"data":..,"error":..}

help.name: process-fds
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-fds    (also: process fds)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage:
  process-fds --pid N [--type KIND] [--target-text SUB] [--offset N] [--limit N] [--max-visited N]
  process fds PID [filters]

Reads one bounded native descriptor inventory between matching process-start identities. Native scan truncation, read errors, filter matches and caller pagination are reported separately. Darwin uses linked libproc code; Linux reads procfs; Windows returns a typed unsupported result rather than using private handle-table layouts.

help.name: process-maps
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-maps    (also: process maps)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage:
  process-maps --pid N [--path SUB] [--permissions rwx] [--executable-only] [--offset N] [--limit N] [--max-visited N]
  process maps PID [filters]

Reads one bounded native virtual-memory inventory between matching process-start identities. Addresses and counters are emitted as decimal/hex strings so JavaScript retains full precision. Non-UTF-8 native paths remain explicitly encoded instead of lossily replaced.

help.name: process-threads
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-threads    (also: process threads)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage:
  process-threads --pid N [--name SUB] [--state STATE] [--offset N] [--limit N] [--max-visited N]
  process threads PID [filters]

Reads one bounded native thread inventory between matching process-start identities. Thread ids and time counters are lossless strings, and time_unit names the platform counter domain. Scan errors and truncation remain visible.

help.name: process-sockets
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-sockets    (also: process sockets)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage:
  process-sockets --pid N [--family FAMILY] [--protocol PROTOCOL] [--state STATE] [--endpoint SUB] [--offset N] [--limit N] [--max-visited N]
  process sockets PID [filters]

Reads one bounded process-owned socket inventory between matching process-start identities. Darwin uses linked libproc and Linux joins /proc/PID/fd socket inodes to the process network namespace without lsof or another executable. Endpoint and Unix-domain path bytes remain lossless. Windows refuses with a typed unsupported result. Native scan truncation, read errors, filter matches and caller pagination remain separate. Watch/diff is not part of this one-shot command.

help.name: process-signal
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-signal    (also: process signal, signal)
  scope: actuate    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  process-signal --pid N SIGNAL [--start-identity ID] [--timeout-ms N] [--force] [--tree --max N]
  process signal PID SIGNAL [--start-identity ID] [--timeout-ms N] [--force] [--tree --max N]
  signal PID SIGNAL [--start-identity ID] [--timeout-ms N] [--force] [--tree --max N]

SIGNAL is one of HUP, INT, TERM, KILL, STOP, CONT, USR1 or USR2 (the SIG prefix is optional). The executor opens mutation-capable native process references before binding live start identities and never uses a naked PID as effect authority. TERM/KILL require exact-object exit read-back; STOP/CONT require scheduler-state read-back. HUP/INT/USR1/USR2 prove exact native delivery but remain verified=false because only the target application can acknowledge their meaning. SIGKILL requires --force. --tree freezes the root and every bounded descendant until two complete snapshots agree, delivers deepest-first, and restores only members it found running; pre-stopped members stay stopped. Linux uses pidfd_send_signal, macOS uses retained audit tokens, and Windows refuses arbitrary trees because it has no retained containment object for pre-existing processes. Privileged signal shapes remain a separate consent-provider gap.

help.text:
agenterm-cu capabilities    (also: caps)

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):

What the selected target can observe and actuate, verb group by verb

help.name: permissions
help.text:
agenterm-cu permissions
  scope: observe    family: System & permissions

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  permissions

Reports the current host's permission model without opening settings or
claiming a grant that the platform cannot inspect. Each permission names the verbs it gates and
the exact repair surface when one exists. This is a read-only status facade; system consent stays
with the user and `permissions` never attempts to bypass it.

help.name: doctor
help.text:
agenterm-cu doctor
  scope: observe    family: System & permissions

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  doctor

Reuses the canonical capabilities and permissions declarations, then
runs bounded window and display inventory probes. A failed probe remains a typed check in the
successful diagnostic document; `doctor` never mutates setup, consent, helpers or foreground state.

help.name: host-open
help.text:
agenterm-cu host-open    (also: open)
  scope: actuate    family: System & permissions

usage: host-open TARGET [--app APPLICATION] [--background]

Dispatches one path or URL through the host's registered application mechanism without a shell. A successful reply proves only that the native dispatcher accepted the request: accepted=true, performed=true, verified=false. It never claims that a handler rendered or consumed the target. Explicit application selection is currently macOS-only; unsupported shapes fail typed instead of being ignored.

help.name: host-notify

agenterm-cu host-notify    (also: notify)

usage: host-notify TITLE [BODY] [--subtitle TEXT] [--sound]

Dispatches bounded notification text without a shell. The durable receipt contains lengths and digests rather than plaintext. accepted=true proves only that the host dispatcher accepted the request; verified remains false because user presentation and attention are not observable. Subtitle and sound are currently macOS-only; unsupported shapes fail typed instead of being ignored.
