help.name: network-interfaces
help.text:
agenterm-cu network-interfaces    (also: network interfaces)
  scope: observe    family: Network

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  network-interfaces [--max N]
  network interfaces [--max N]

arguments:
  --max N                       returned address rows, 1..=5000 (default 1000)

Enumerates native IPv4 and IPv6 interface addresses without invoking a shell.
Rows carry the platform's native interface identity, address, prefix/netmask,
MAC when available, loopback state and IPv6 scope. Results are stable-sorted
and bounded; scan truncation, response truncation and per-row read errors stay
explicit instead of making a partial snapshot look complete.

help.name: network-probe
help.text:
agenterm-cu network-probe    (also: network probe)
  scope: observe    family: Network

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  network-probe HOST [--port N] [--attempts N] [--timeout-ms N]
  network probe HOST [--port N] [--attempts N] [--timeout-ms N]

arguments:
  HOST                          bare hostname or IP address
  --port N                      TCP port, 1..=65535 (default 443)
  --attempts N                  exact attempts, 1..=20 (default 3)
  --timeout-ms N                resolver and per-connect bound, 100..=60000 (default 3000)

Resolves through the host resolver once, deduplicates and freezes the
address set, then makes the exact requested number of TCP attempts round-robin.
The blocking resolver lives in an invocation-owned internal child; the parent
enforces the overall deadline and kills and reaps that child on expiry. A TCP
refusal or timeout is a successful unreachable observation. Resolver, worker
and protocol failures stay typed. This is reachability evidence, not HTTP/TLS.

help.name: file-inspect
help.text:
agenterm-cu file-inspect    (also: file inspect)
  scope: observe    family: Filesystem

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  file-inspect PATH
  file inspect PATH

arguments:
  PATH                          one file, directory, or link-like entry

Reads bounded metadata for exactly the final entry without following a final
link. The reply carries kind, lossless decimal size and timestamps, readonly
state, platform metadata, and a stable opened-object identity for ordinary
files and directories. Link-object identity is available from Unix metadata;
Windows reports that identity as typed unavailable instead of following the
link. No file contents are read.

help.name: file-copy
help.text:
agenterm-cu file-copy    (also: file copy)
  scope: observe for plan; actuate for --apply    family: Filesystem

usage (after the global flags):
  file-copy SOURCE DESTINATION [--replace] [--apply]
  file copy SOURCE DESTINATION [--replace] [--apply]

The default is a mutation-free plan. It snapshots an opened, non-symlink regular source and any existing regular destination by identity, size, modification time, permissions and SHA-256. --apply reserves a private recovery receipt before mutation, serializes the exact destination across processes, publishes a verified same-directory temporary with source permissions, and keeps a replaced destination as a backup until finalize. The receipt reports destination_durable=false if publication became visible but parent-directory durability could not be confirmed. --replace is mandatory when the destination exists. File contents are never returned.

help.name: file-move
help.text:
agenterm-cu file-move    (also: file move)
  scope: observe for plan; actuate for --apply    family: Filesystem

usage (after the global flags):
  file-move SOURCE DESTINATION [--replace] [--apply]
  file move SOURCE DESTINATION [--replace] [--apply]

The default is a mutation-free plan with the same identity, size, modification time, permissions and SHA-256 snapshots as file-copy. --apply reserves a private recovery receipt before mutation, takes the cross-process locks for both exact paths, publishes a verified same-directory temporary at the destination, retains a replaced destination as a backup, then retires the source into a same-directory source backup. Both backups stay until finalize, so rollback restores the exact recorded source and destination objects. Copying then retiring keeps one recoverable path for same-volume and cross-volume moves. --replace is mandatory when the destination exists. File contents are never returned.

help.name: file-transaction
help.text:
agenterm-cu file-transaction    (also: file status|rollback|recover|finalize)
  scope: observe for status; actuate for mutation    family: Filesystem

usage (after the global flags):
  file-transaction status|rollback|recover|finalize TRANSACTION_ID
  file status|rollback|recover|finalize TRANSACTION_ID

The receipt operation (file.copy or file.move) selects the owner. status returns the durable receipt without file content. rollback restores the exact recorded prior destination (and, for a move, the retired source) or removes a newly installed destination. recover reconciles reserved, partial-copy, backup-moved, installed-before-receipt and installed-before-retire crash windows. finalize verifies the completed post-state and deletes the retained backups. Every operation takes the same path locks as apply and refuses changed or ambiguous state with a typed error.

help.name: windows
help.text:
agenterm-cu windows    (also: focused-window)
  scope: observe    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  windows [--pid N] [--app SUB] [--title SUB] [--focused [BOOL]] [--minimized [BOOL]]
          [--browser-profile SUB] [--offset N] [--max N]
  focused-window                                      (= windows --focused true)

arguments:
  --pid N                       owning process id
  --app SUB                     application name substring
  --title SUB                   window title substring
  --focused [BOOL]              only the focused window (true, default; reply adds focused_app + window) or unfocused windows
  --minimized [BOOL]            only minimized (true, default) or shown windows
  --browser-profile SUB         case-insensitive substring of the window's browser_profile (Chromium profile name)
  --offset N                    page start
  --max N                       page size

Bare: the window array. With any filter or page flag the reply is
{windows, visited, matched, returned, offset, truncated}. Browser rows
carry browser_profile (the Chromium profile name from the window's
" - <App> - <profile>" identity suffix, read from the AX root when the
inventory title lacks it; the <App> segment is matched loosely against
app_name, because only macOS reports a display name there -- Linux
reports /proc/<pid>/comm and Windows the image name);
--browser-profile SUB keeps only those rows
(case-insensitive substring), so an agent can address one profile's
window of a multi-profile instance. Focus: the mechanism's own mark is
kept when it made one; otherwise the frontmost application (NSWorkspace
on macOS) decides -- its own AXFocusedWindow, else its topmost window in
the stacking order -- because the system-wide accessibility focus read
fails from a process outside the GUI front chain (tmux, SSH, an agent
bridge). Every object reply carries focus: {handle, via, reason}; with
--focused true (alias focused-window) it also carries focused_app
{name, pid, bundle_id} and window (the row, or null with reason
frontmost_app_has_no_inventory_window / no_frontmost_app), so a
"front window unchanged" check never reads an empty list as "none".

help.name: windows-watch
help.text:
agenterm-cu windows-watch
  scope: observe    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  windows-watch [--pid N] [--app SUB] [--title SUB] [--duration-ms N] [--interval-ms N]
                [--max-events N]

arguments:
  --pid N                       owning process id
  --app SUB                     application name substring
  --title SUB                   window title substring
  --duration-ms N               watch window; 0 (default) takes one extra sample
  --interval-ms N               poll interval
  --max-events N                stop after N events

poll-diff over the windows inventory (appeared / disappeared / changed +
field list). Not AXObserver. --duration-ms 0 (default) takes one extra
sample.

help.name: apps
help.text:
agenterm-cu apps
  scope: observe    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  apps [--running] [--all]

arguments:
  --running                     running applications only (the default set)
  --all                         also the installed applications no window can reveal

Running apps from top-level windows (pids + window count). --all also
lists the applications installed on this host that no window can reveal,
each marked running or not.

help.name: ps
help.text:
agenterm-cu ps
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  ps [--pid N] [--parent N] [--name SUB] [--offset N] [--max N]

arguments:
  --pid N                       exact process id
  --parent N                    exact parent process id
  --name SUB                    case-insensitive executable-name substring
  --offset N                    page start
  --max N                       page size

Lists process id, parent id and executable name through the same
agenterm-platform process facade used by qjswasm process.list. Results are
sorted by pid and bounded before publication. MCU's --command, CPU, memory,
file and port filters remain typed migration gaps until their owning facades
land; this command never silently ignores them.

help.name: process-state
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-state    (also: process state)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  process-state --pid N
  process state --pid N

arguments:
  --pid N                       positive process id to observe

Returns live, dead, or unknown through the shared process-observation
facade. A live result includes the platform start identity when available.
Unknown is fail-closed and never means dead. Future mutation commands must bind
their target to this identity rather than trusting a reusable pid alone.

help.name: process-argv
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-argv    (also: process argv)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  process-argv --pid N [--offset N] [--limit N] [--values]
  process argv PID [--offset N] [--limit N] [--values]

arguments:
  --pid N                       positive process id (or positional PID)
  --offset N                    first argument index (default 0)
  --limit N                     returned arguments, 1..=4096 (default 100)
  --values                      explicitly include argument text

Reads the native bounded argv vector between two matching process-start
identity observations. The executable path is always visible. By default each
argument contains only its index, UTF-8 byte length and SHA-256; plaintext is
returned only with --values. Pagination is explicit and reports truncation.
A process exit, PID reuse, denied provider or oversized native buffer fails
typed instead of returning a partial or different process.

help.name: process-usage
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-usage    (also: process usage)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  process-usage --pid N [--watch-ms N --interval-ms N --max-samples N]
  process usage --pid N [--watch-ms N --interval-ms N --max-samples N]

arguments:
  --pid N                       positive process id to sample
  --watch-ms N                  bounded observation duration, 1..=86400000
  --interval-ms N               sample interval, 1..=60000 (default 1000)
  --max-samples N               maximum returned samples, 1..=4096 (default 120)

Reads one cumulative resource sample between two matching process-start
identity observations. CPU nanoseconds, resident bytes and page-fault counters
are decimal strings so JSON/JavaScript consumers cannot lose u64 precision.
Watch mode takes an immediate sample, then samples on a monotonic bounded
schedule while the same start identity remains live. It reports every sample
and whether the sample ceiling truncated the requested duration. Richer I/O
counters remain an explicit migration gap.

help.name: process-wait
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-wait    (also: process wait)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  process-wait --pid N --start-identity ID [--timeout-ms N]
  process wait --pid N --start-identity ID [--timeout-ms N]

arguments:
  --pid N                       positive process id previously observed
  --start-identity ID           exact value returned by process-state
  --timeout-ms N                monotonic wait limit, 1..=86400000 (default 30000)

Opens a native stable process reference, verifies that its current start
identity equals the caller's prior process-state observation, then waits for
that exact process object. A timeout is a verified live result, not an error;
an identity mismatch fails before waiting. This avoids MCU's repeated PID
        polling and cannot silently follow a recycled pid.

help.name: process-kill
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-kill    (also: process kill, kill)
  scope: actuate    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  process-kill --pid N --start-identity ID [--mode forceful|graceful] [--timeout-ms N] --expect exited
  kill PID --start-identity ID [--mode forceful|graceful] [--timeout-ms N] --expect exited

arguments:
  --pid N                       positive process id previously observed
  --start-identity ID           exact value returned by process-state
  --mode MODE                   forceful (default) or graceful
  --timeout-ms N                monotonic exit-verification limit, 1..=86400000 (default 30000)
  --expect exited               required destructive postcondition

Opens a mutation-capable native reference, checks its start identity
against the caller's prior observation, reserves a crash-persistent receipt,
terminates through that exact object, then waits on the same object for exit.
Linux uses pidfd_send_signal and Windows forceful mode uses the retained HANDLE.
macOS refuses the operation because kqueue observation cannot make a later PID
signal atomic against PID reuse. Graceful mode is therefore Linux-only today;
unsupported is typed and no naked-PID fallback is allowed.

help.name: process-watch
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-watch    (also: process watch)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  process-watch [--pid N] [--parent N] [--name SUB] [--all] [--duration-ms N --interval-ms N --max-events N --max-processes N]
  process watch [selectors] [limits]

arguments:
  --pid N                       watch one process id
  --parent N                    watch direct children of one parent
  --name SUB                    watch executable-name substring
  --all                         watch the whole bounded inventory
  --duration-ms N               monotonic duration, 1..=86400000 (default 30000)
  --interval-ms N               poll interval, 1..=60000 (default 1000)
  --max-events N                event ceiling, 1..=4096 (default 256)
  --max-processes N             matched inventory ceiling, 1..=5000 (default 1000)

Takes an immediate baseline, then emits started/exited diffs until the
monotonic duration or event ceiling is reached. Every row carries a native
start identity; pid reuse therefore appears as an exit plus a start. An
unverifiable identity on an exact PID fails closed. A broad selector excludes
unidentified processes and reports `coverage_complete: false` plus the count;
it never degrades those rows to pid-only polling. Oversized inventory fails
closed.

help.name: shell-exec
help.text:
agenterm-cu shell-exec
  scope: actuate    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  shell-exec --command TEXT [--timeout-ms N] [--max-output-bytes N]

Runs one host-shell command through /bin/sh on Unix or PowerShell on Windows. The root is contained before its first instruction; timeout and output-limit failures terminate and reap the owned tree or return cleanup_uncertain. stdout and stderr are drained concurrently under one aggregate byte ceiling. A non-zero shell exit is a completed ok=true observation with success=false and its exact exit fact; transport exec --json remains a separate worker mode.

help.name: pty-start
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-start    (also: pty start)
  scope: actuate    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-start NAME [--cwd DIR] -- PROGRAM ARG...
  pty start NAME [--cwd DIR] -- PROGRAM ARG...

Starts one invisible, cross-process PTY job under a deterministic isolated AgenTerm logical instance. AgenTerm server remains the sole POSIX PTY/ConPTY, terminal-tree, retention and process-lifecycle owner. NAME is 1..=64 ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen. The command is typed argv, never a shell string; its values are not copied into receipts. A same-name concurrent or existing job fails typed.

help.name: pty-list
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-list    (also: pty list)
  scope: observe    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-list
  pty list

Enumerates the bounded private named-job state directory, sorts names, and reconciles each entry with its deterministic AgenTerm authority. A row is running with full epoch/tab/process status, stale when no authority is reachable, or conflicted with a typed reconciliation error. Symlinks, malformed names and more than 4096 entries fail closed; this read-only verb never deletes or starts a job.

help.name: pty-prune
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-prune    (also: pty prune)
  scope: actuate    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-prune NAME --expect stale
  pty prune NAME --expect stale

Reclaims one exact named state directory only after taking the same registry lock as pty-start, taking the job lock, and independently proving that the deterministic authority is unreachable. It reserves a persistent receipt before deletion, accepts only the known workspace/settings/lock files, removes no unknown subtree, and verifies the directory is absent. A live or conflicted authority, unknown entry, link-like directory, concurrent start, missing intent or missing state fails typed without deletion.

help.name: pty-status
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-status    (also: pty status)
  scope: observe    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-status NAME
  pty status NAME

Returns the durable job identity (name + server scope + epoch + stable @tab), process id, terminal dimensions, dead/finalized state and exit code. A missing authority or an authority that does not contain exactly one job tab fails typed.

help.name: pty-read
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-read    (also: pty read)
  scope: observe    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-read NAME [--cursor earliest|current|N] [--max-bytes N]
  pty read NAME ...

Reads the same retained redacted raw PTY byte ring as terminal-output. Base64 is lossless; valid UTF-8 is auxiliary. Continue from next_cursor. Overwritten and future cursors fail typed rather than silently skipping bytes.

help.name: pty-snapshot
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-snapshot    (also: pty snapshot)
  scope: observe    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-snapshot NAME
  pty snapshot NAME

Returns the sole durable job tab's bounded structured screen plus the exact server epoch and ordered event cursor. It also persists a bounded baseline beside the audit log and returns snapshot_id. The job name, logical server scope, epoch and stable tab id remain one identity; an epoch change during capture fails typed rather than publishing a substituted snapshot. Continue with pty-events or pty-diff.

help.name: pty-diff
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-diff    (also: pty diff)
  scope: observe    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-diff NAME --base SNAPSHOT_ID [--advance] [--max N]
  pty diff NAME --base SNAPSHOT_ID [--advance] [--max N]

Loads one persisted bounded screen baseline and captures the named job again. Success requires the same job, server scope, epoch and stable tab id; restart fails pty_snapshot_authority_changed instead of comparing unrelated terminals. The reply separates changed rows from terminal metadata changes and bounds rows with --max. --advance publishes the current capture as next_base in the same operation. The private store keeps at most 128 baselines total and each record is capped at 2 MiB.

help.name: pty-events
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-events    (also: pty events)
  scope: observe    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-events NAME --epoch EPOCH --after SEQUENCE [--limit N]
  pty events NAME --epoch EPOCH --after SEQUENCE [--limit N]

Continues the bounded ordered UI event journal for the sole tab of an exact durable job. The supplied epoch must still match the named authority. Its cursor advances across every scanned event while returned terminal updates remain filtered to the job tab, preventing unrelated activity from trapping the caller in replay. Restart, overwritten history and future cursors fail typed.

help.name: pty-resize
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-resize    (also: pty resize)
  scope: actuate    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-resize NAME --rows ROWS --columns COLUMNS
  pty resize NAME --rows ROWS --columns COLUMNS

Acquires a temporary UI lease on the exact dedicated headless authority, resizes its sole tab, detaches the lease and independently reads the job status back. Success requires the same server epoch and tab plus the exact requested 1..=512 grid. The job lock serializes concurrent mutations; a failed detach or mismatched read-back is typed and retained in a crash-persistent receipt.

help.name: pty-send
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-send    (also: pty send)
  scope: actuate    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-send NAME -- TEXT
  pty send NAME -- TEXT

Sends one non-empty literal UTF-8 argument to the exact epoch-scoped job tab and requires AgenTerm's committed control receipt. No Enter or shell interpretation is implicit; include \r or \n in TEXT when the target program requires it. Same-name mutations are serialized.

help.name: pty-wait
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-wait    (also: pty wait)
  scope: observe    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-wait NAME --contains TEXT [--cursor earliest|current|N] [--timeout-ms N]
  pty wait NAME ...

Waits for exact UTF-8 bytes in the loss-aware retained raw-output stream, including a match split across output pages. The reply reports its byte cursor and scan count. Overwritten/future cursors, timeout, and finalized-without-match are distinct typed failures; output is never reduced to a screen snapshot.

help.name: pty-wait-exit
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-wait-exit    (also: pty wait-exit)
  scope: observe    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-wait-exit NAME [--timeout-ms N] [--expect-status N]
  pty wait-exit NAME ...

Waits with a monotonic deadline until both the child and the terminal reader are finalized, then reads the exact exit status. An optional 0..=255 expected status is verified; timeout or mismatch is a typed nonzero failure.

help.name: pty-stop
help.text:
agenterm-cu pty-stop    (also: pty stop)
  scope: actuate    family: Headless PTY jobs

usage:
  pty-stop NAME --expect stopped
  pty stop NAME --expect stopped

Requires the explicit destructive postcondition, closes the exact epoch-scoped job tab through AgenTerm's own lifecycle, asks the now-empty authority to shut down, and verifies that its IPC endpoint disappears.

help.name: terminal-list
help.text:
agenterm-cu terminal-list    (also: terminal list)
  scope: observe    family: AgenTerm terminals

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  terminal-list
  terminal list

Returns the product control plane's structured ui-bootstrap
inventory. A reliable identity is server_scope_id + server_epoch + tab @N;
index and title are mutable human labels, not authority.

help.name: terminal-new
help.text:
agenterm-cu terminal-new    (also: terminal new)
  scope: actuate    family: AgenTerm terminals

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  terminal-new [--title TEXT] [--parent @N] [--detached] [-- PROGRAM ARG...]
  terminal new [options]

arguments:
  --title TEXT                  optional title, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes
  --parent @N                   optional stable parent id from terminal-list
  --detached                    do not select the new tab
  -- PROGRAM ARG...             exact child command, at most 256 args / 1048576 bytes

Reserves a crash-persistent receipt, calls AgenTerm's existing new-window
control operation, then proves the returned @N exists in the same server scope
and epoch. Parent identity is read back when supplied. Command values and title
text are not copied into the receipt; only bounded byte counts are retained.

help.name: terminal-close
help.text:
agenterm-cu terminal-close    (also: terminal close)
  scope: actuate    family: AgenTerm terminals

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  terminal-close --tab @N --expect closed
  terminal close --tab @N --expect closed

arguments:
  --tab @N                      exact stable tab id from terminal-list
  --expect closed               required destructive postcondition

Reserves a crash-persistent receipt, invokes the product's bounded kill-window
operation, then proves that exact @N is absent in the same server epoch. AgenTerm
owns child shutdown, parent promotion and last-tab behavior; ACU does not fake
tmux session semantics or terminate the application window itself.

help.name: terminal-read
help.text:
agenterm-cu terminal-read    (also: terminal read)
  scope: observe    family: AgenTerm terminals

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  terminal-read --tab @N [--max-bytes N]
  terminal read --tab @N [--max-bytes N]

arguments:
  --tab @N                      stable tab id from terminal-list
  --max-bytes N                 UTF-8 response ceiling, 1..=1048576 (default 262144)

Reads vt100 screen contents through capture-pane --json.
This is a bounded screen snapshot, not an incremental raw-output cursor; the
reply says so explicitly and never invents byte-range parity.

help.name: terminal-send
help.text:
agenterm-cu terminal-send    (also: terminal send)
  scope: actuate    family: AgenTerm terminals

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  terminal-send --tab @N -- TEXT
  terminal send --tab @N -- TEXT

arguments:
  --tab @N                      stable tab id from terminal-list
  --                            end options; remaining text is sent literally

Uses AgenTerm's own send-keys -l control operation. It
reserves an ACU receipt before sending and retains the server control receipt;
dead/non-writable tabs fail typed instead of falling back to desktop typing.

help.name: terminal-snapshot
help.text:
agenterm-cu terminal-snapshot    (also: terminal snapshot)
  scope: observe    family: AgenTerm terminals

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  terminal-snapshot --tab @N
  terminal snapshot --tab @N

arguments:
  --tab @N                      stable tab id from terminal-list

Returns one bounded structured screen, including cell runs, styles, cursor,
terminal modes and completeness flags, together with server_scope_id and an
exact {server_epoch, sequence} cursor. This is an event-journal cursor, not a
raw PTY byte offset. Continue it with terminal-events.

help.name: terminal-events
help.text:
agenterm-cu terminal-events    (also: terminal events)
  scope: observe    family: AgenTerm terminals

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  terminal-events --tab @N --epoch EPOCH --after SEQUENCE [--limit N]
  terminal events --tab @N --epoch EPOCH --after SEQUENCE [--limit N]

arguments:
  --tab @N                      stable tab id from terminal-snapshot
  --epoch EPOCH                 exact server epoch from terminal-snapshot
  --after SEQUENCE              last consumed event sequence
  --limit N                     events scanned per page, 1..=64 (default 64)

Reads AgenTerm's bounded ordered UI delta journal. Restart, overwritten history
and a future sequence fail typed. The reply filters published events and screen
updates to the requested tab, but advances its cursor across every scanned
event so unrelated tabs cannot trap a reader in an infinite replay loop.
complete/truncated say whether the cursor reached the current server position.

help.name: terminal-output
help.text:
agenterm-cu terminal-output    (also: terminal output)
  scope: observe    family: AgenTerm terminals

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  terminal-output --tab @N [--cursor earliest|current|N] [--max-bytes N]
  terminal output --tab @N ...

arguments:
  --tab @N                      stable tab id from terminal-list
  --cursor CURSOR               earliest/current bootstrap or prior next_cursor (default earliest)
  --max-bytes N                 bounded page size, 1..=1048576 (default 65536)

Reads the retained redacted raw PTY byte stream without UTF-8 loss. The reply
always carries base64 plus cursor bounds; valid UTF-8 pages also carry utf8.
Continue from next_cursor. A cursor older than earliest_cursor fails typed as
terminal_output_gap, and a cursor beyond current_cursor fails typed as
terminal_output_future_cursor. This cursor is independent of terminal-events.

help.name: terminal-wait
help.text:
agenterm-cu terminal-wait    (also: terminal wait)
  scope: observe    family: AgenTerm terminals

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  terminal-wait --tab @N (--contains TEXT|--exited|--finalized) [--timeout-ms N]
  terminal wait --tab @N ...

arguments:
  --tab @N                      stable tab id from terminal-list
  --contains TEXT               current screen contains text
  --exited                      child exit code is present
  --finalized                   child exited and reader/parser tail drained
  --timeout-ms N                monotonic deadline, 1..=86400000 (default 5000)

Polls the typed control plane at 50 ms with a monotonic
deadline. Exactly one condition is required. --finalized is stronger than
--exited and should precede a final read when late PTY output matters.

help.name: app
help.text:
agenterm-cu app    (also: launch, quit, hide, show)
  scope: actuate    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  app <hide|show|quit|launch> [--window HANDLE] [--pid N] [--path P] [--snapshot --expect gone]
  hide|show|quit --window HANDLE | --pid N        (alias of app <action>)
  launch PATH | launch --path PATH                (alias of app launch)

arguments:
  <action>                      hide | show | quit | launch (or --action <one of them>)
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --pid N                       process id; show needs it because hiding removed the windows
  --path P                      launch: installed application path
  --snapshot                    write the bounded tree to the receipt before acting
  --expect gone                 checkable postcondition: the handle reads back as absent

Steps a whole application, not one of its windows. hide/show take it
aside and back (show takes --pid: hiding removed the windows the handle
named); quit is destructive and carries the same three-part gate as close
-- it presses the application's own Quit item and reads the process back.
launch --path starts an installed application; the reply says pid: null
because the launcher owns the process, so wait for its window if a pid is
needed. `launch PATH`, `quit`, `hide` and `show` are the MCU spellings of
`app <action>`.

help.name: unlock
help.text:
agenterm-cu unlock
  scope: observe    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  unlock --window HANDLE

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)

Asks the owning application to build its full accessibility tree,
reading the bounded tree before and after. The poke is per host and the
reply's poke field names the one that ran: macOS sets AXManualAccessibility
(plus AXEnhancedUserInterface on the application); Linux flips the
desktop-wide org.a11y.Status switch (IsEnabled + ScreenReaderEnabled on the
session-bus name org.a11y.Bus) that a Chromium renderer watches before it
publishes a web tree; Windows has no separate poke to make, because a
Chromium process turns accessibility on when it answers WM_GETOBJECT for
its window and the UIA tree walk sends that itself -- there poked is false
WITH a reason, which is not a failure.

Reports poked (the request was delivered), grew and returned_before
separately, because the poke's own status is not the outcome: AppKit calls
the attribute unsupported even when it lands, and the Linux flags may
already be set, so only the re-read can claim anything about the tree.

Evidence: macOS is proven on a real Brave instance
(scripts/cu-brave-live-smoke.sh). The Linux and Windows paths are
code-complete but have no live run yet; scripts/cu-linux-smoke.sh and
scripts/qjs/cu-windows-browser-smoke.qjs carry the journey and exit with a
typed SKIP until a host with a Chromium-family browser runs them.

help.name: close
help.text:
agenterm-cu close
  scope: actuate    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  close --window HANDLE [--pid N] [--title T] --snapshot --expect gone

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --pid N                       bind the handle to this process in the same inventory read
  --title T                     bind the handle to this exact title in the same inventory read
  --snapshot                    write the bounded tree to the receipt before acting
  --expect gone                 checkable postcondition: the handle reads back as absent

The destructive verb: closes one top-level window in the background
through the platform's own close control (macOS AXCloseButton + AXPress).
The gate is three parts, all checked before anything is touched: an exact
target (--window, bound to --pid / exact --title in the same inventory
read), a prior snapshot (--snapshot: the bounded tree written to the
receipt) and a checkable postcondition (--expect gone: the handle read back
as absent). Missing any -> "refused" (detail.reason destructive_gate,
missing [...]) with nothing performed.

help.name: activate
help.text:
agenterm-cu activate
  scope: actuate    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  activate --window HANDLE

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)

Makes one exact top-level window the desktop foreground owner and
then polls the public window inventory until that exact handle reads
focused. This is the whole-window operation MCU spells `focus HANDLE`.

It is deliberately not `focus`, which targets one accessibility node
inside a window, and not `raise`, which changes only an application's own
window order without activating the application. A mechanism refusal or
missing focused read-back fails typed; sending an activation request is
not by itself success.

help.name: raise
help.text:
agenterm-cu raise
  scope: actuate    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  raise --window HANDLE

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)

Lifts one window in front of the other windows OF ITS OWN APPLICATION
(macOS: AXRaise on the window element), then reads that order back. It
does not activate the application and does not change the system
frontmost application: the frontmost pid is read before and after and the
reply carries both plus frontmost_app_unchanged. If it moved anyway, the
verb fails typed "foreground_changed" rather than reporting success.

raise is NOT focus. `focus` gives one accessibility NODE inside a window
the keyboard focus and never touches stacking; `raise` moves a whole
WINDOW in front of its siblings and never moves the accessibility focus.
Neither is `orderwin`, which orders one window against another named
window in the DESKTOP-wide order.

Verification is the application-local stacking read-back: rank 0 of its
app's windows. A host that reports no stacking order answers verified
false with reason stacking_unreadable rather than letting the absence of
a contradiction read as success; a window the order refuses to move
fails typed "window_order_not_applied".

help.name: minimize
help.text:
agenterm-cu minimize
  scope: actuate    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  minimize --window HANDLE --expect minimized

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --expect minimized            checkable postcondition: the window reads back minimized

Sends one window to the dock through the window's own minimize
affordance (macOS: the window attribute AXMinimized set to true). Never a
keyboard shortcut, never by activating the application; the frontmost pid
is read before and after and reported.

Gated like `close`, minus the snapshot: an exact target (--window HANDLE)
and a checkable postcondition (--expect minimized). Missing either ->
"refused" (detail.reason destructive_gate, missing [...]) with nothing
performed. A window that is ALREADY minimized is a verified no-op
(performed false, verified true, reason already_minimized) -- the same
contract `invoke set-checked` has for a state that already holds.

Read-back is the window's own minimized state, polled until it settles.
Note for macOS: the `windows` inventory is on-screen only, so a minimized
window LEAVES it rather than appearing with minimized true; the reply
reports both after.minimized (the window's own state) and
after.inventory_present so the two are never confused.

help.name: restore
help.text:
agenterm-cu restore
  scope: actuate    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  restore --window HANDLE --expect restored

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --expect restored             checkable postcondition: the window reads back not minimized

Brings one minimized window back (macOS: AXMinimized set to false)
without activating its application. Same gate as `minimize` with
--expect restored, the same already-restored verified no-op, and the same
minimized read-back; the window handle is stable across minimize and
restore, so the handle `windows` gave before the minimize is the one to
pass here.

help.name: receipts
help.text:
agenterm-cu receipts
  scope: observe    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  receipts [--window HANDLE] [--max N]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --max N                       lines to return (default 50, at most 1000)

The target's crash-persistent receipt file (<audit dir>/cu-receipts/
<target>.jsonl) read back in order: every invoke / menu invoke / click /
focus / close appends a "reserved" line before the mechanism and a
"completed" / "failed" line after the read-back; a "reserved" line with no
partner is the crash signature (uncertain, never "did not happen").
Default 50, at most 1000.

help.name: spaces
help.text:
agenterm-cu spaces
  scope: observe    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  spaces

macOS SkyLight managed Space inventory (read-only). linux/windows answer
typed unsupported.

help.name: displays
help.text:
agenterm-cu displays
  scope: observe    family: Windows & apps

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  displays

Native screen frames via agt_screen_list (MCU system group).

help.name: tree
help.text:
agenterm-cu tree    (also: elements)
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  tree [--window HANDLE] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--flat]
  elements [--window HANDLE] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N]     (alias of tree --flat)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --depth N                     walk depth (root = 0, at most 64)
  --max-nodes N                 node budget while the platform walks (1..20000)
  --flat                        number nodes (index, depth) in walk order

Depth (root=0, <=64) and node budget (1..20000) apply while the platform
walks; the reply carries truncated / visited / returned. --flat numbers
nodes (index, depth) in walk order -- the same identity query reports.
`elements` is the MCU spelling of tree --flat.

help.name: desktop-state
help.text:
agenterm-cu desktop-state    (also: state)
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  desktop-state [--window HANDLE] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N]
  state [--window HANDLE] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N]     (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               exact window from `windows`; omitted only when focus resolves uniquely
  --depth N                     tree walk depth (root = 0, at most 64)
  --max-nodes N                 node budget while the platform walks (1..20000)

Composes one bounded top-level window inventory, one selected window's bounded
accessibility tree, and the absolute pointer position. It never captures a
screenshot. An explicit handle must be in the first inventory; an omitted handle
requires a unique resolved focused window. The target is re-enumerated after the
tree read and any changed/disappeared row fails typed `desktop_state_changed`.
The tree says whether its node bound truncated; a desktop with more than 512
windows refuses rather than returning a partial inventory.

help.name: query
help.text:
agenterm-cu query    (also: inspect, find, read)
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  query --window HANDLE|App#N | HANDLE [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--role R,R]
        [--text T | --text-exact T] [--identifier ID] [--actionable] [--within X,Y,W,H]
        [--offset N] [--max N] [--selector PATH]
  inspect HANDLE [flags]           (alias of query; --app is a migration gap)
  find HANDLE TEXT [flags]         (alias of query --text TEXT)
  read HANDLE SELECTOR [flags]     (alias of query --selector SELECTOR)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --depth N                     walk depth (root = 0, at most 64)
  --max-nodes N                 node budget while the platform walks (1..20000)
  --role R,R                    roles to keep (AXTextArea or text-area spellings)
  --text T                      name / value substring
  --text-exact T                exact name / value (not with --text)
  --identifier ID               accessibility identifier
  --actionable                  nodes that offer an action
  --within X,Y,W,H              screen rectangle the node must intersect
  --offset N                    page start
  --max N                       page size
  --selector PATH               MCU Role[idx] / Role@title / *@title / #desc path

Bounded, filtered flat node list with visited / matched / returned /
truncated; roles accept AXTextArea or text-area; an unknown flag fails
before the walk. inspect is query (MCU `inspect HANDLE`; `--app` stays
MCU). find HANDLE TEXT is query --text; read HANDLE SELECTOR is query
--selector. MCU selectors: Role[idx] / Role@title / *@title / #desc.

help.name: hit
help.text:
agenterm-cu hit
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  hit --window HANDLE --x X --y Y [--depth N] [--max-nodes N]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --x X                         screen x (the space node bounds and query --within use)
  --y Y                         screen y
  --depth N                     walk depth (root = 0, at most 64)
  --max-nodes N                 node budget while the platform walks (1..20000)

Screen coordinates -> the node under them, in the same shape `query`
returns (index, depth, id, role, name, bounds, ...), so the id goes
straight into invoke --node / click --node. `containing` lists every node
whose rectangle holds the point, so an ambiguous spot is visible rather
than hidden behind the winner.

Ranking: deepest wins, then smallest area, then the later position in
walk order (a sibling drawn afterwards sits on top). A zero-area
rectangle is never a hit. Nothing here reads or moves the pointer.

The point is resolved inside the window's own bounded walk, not through
the platform's point-to-element call (macOS
AXUIElementCopyElementAtPosition): that call returns a live element with
no address in the id space tree / query publish, so its answer could not
be handed to invoke --node -- which is the whole reason to ask. A miss is
typed "a11y_node_not_found" with the walk's visited / truncated counts.

help.name: focused
help.text:
agenterm-cu focused
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  focused --window HANDLE [--role ROLE] [--max-value-bytes N]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --role ROLE                   expected role ("unverified" on mismatch)
  --max-value-bytes N           value preview size (default 4096; 0 keeps only value_bytes)

The application's own focused control inside the window (id / role /
name / identifier / states / value preview), read without the foreground;
--role binds the expected role ("unverified" on mismatch); default preview
4096 bytes, 0 keeps only value_bytes.

help.name: observe
help.text:
agenterm-cu observe
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  observe --window HANDLE (--duration S | --duration-ms N) [--depth N] [--max-nodes N]
          [--max-events N] [--notification A,B] [--interval-ms N] [--mode poll-diff|notifications]
          [--ready-path PATH]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --duration S                  seconds, fractions allowed, within (0, 120]
  --duration-ms N               exact milliseconds (not with --duration)
  --depth N                     walk depth (root = 0, at most 64)
  --max-nodes N                 node budget while the platform walks (1..20000)
  --max-events N                stop after N events (<= 5000, default 200)
  --notification A,B            event kinds to keep
  --interval-ms N               poll interval
  --mode poll-diff|notificationsevent source
  --ready-path PATH             atomic marker after the complete poll-diff baseline

Bounded event stream by poll-diff over the same bounded tree:
ValueChanged / TitleChanged / StateChanged / FocusChanged / Created /
Destroyed with monotonic seq and t_ms; stops at --max-events (<= 5000,
default 200) with truncated true; reports polls / emitted / filtered /
stopped. --ready-path publishes a caller-owned no-overwrite JSON marker
after the complete poll-diff baseline and before its duration starts; native
notifications reject it until subscription readiness is available.

help.name: snapshot
help.text:
agenterm-cu snapshot
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  snapshot --window HANDLE [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--out PATH]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --depth N                     walk depth (root = 0, at most 64)
  --max-nodes N                 node budget while the platform walks (1..20000)
  --out PATH                    also write the baseline itself to this path

Captures the bounded tree once and stores it as a named baseline, so
`diff` can answer "what changed since" without the caller holding the
tree. The reply carries snapshot_id, the node count and truncated.

Baselines live beside the receipts, under the same audit directory:
<audit dir>/cu-snapshots/<target>/w<window>/<snapshot_id>.json, so
AGENTERM_CU_AUDIT_PATH relocates audit, receipts and baselines together.
Each window keeps its 32 newest baselines and older ones are dropped, so
a poll loop cannot grow the store without end.

help.name: diff
help.text:
agenterm-cu diff
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  diff --window HANDLE [--base SNAPSHOT_ID] [--advance] [--max N]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --base SNAPSHOT_ID            baseline to compare against (default: the window's most recent)
  --advance                     store the walk just read as the next baseline
  --max N                       changes per bucket (default 200, at most 2000)

Walks the window again and returns added / removed / changed nodes in
the same shape `query` returns; a changed row carries `changed` with the
names of the fields that differ (role, name, parent_id, states, bounds,
actions, text, identifier). The current walk reuses the BASELINE's budget
so a difference is a difference in the window, never a difference in how
far each side looked.

Without --base the window's most recent baseline is used and
base_selected_by says "most-recent"; base carries the id that was used.
--advance stores the walk it just compared as the next baseline in the
same call, so an agent polls a window with one verb per tick and misses
nothing between replies; next_base names the id to expect.

Node ids are positional paths (/0/3/1) -- which is what makes them
usable with invoke --node -- so inserting a sibling renumbers the ones
after it and one real insertion can read as one added plus several
changed. The field names say which: a renumbered node changes name /
role, a moved one changes only bounds.

Each bucket is capped at --max with truncated set; walk_truncated says
the tree walk itself hit its budget on either side.

help.name: verify
help.text:
agenterm-cu verify
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  verify --window HANDLE --expect '[{"node"|"index"|"name"|"titleIncludes"[+"role"]|"identifier"|"role",
                                     "value"?, "checked"?, "expanded"?, "focused"?}, ...]'

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --expect JSON                 array of closed-shape items; an unknown key is a usage error

One tree read; all met -> ok + verified, a mismatch -> "unverified", a
state the node does not expose -> "unsupported" (fail closed), an unknown
key -> usage. name/titleIncludes alone is page identity (WebArea title).

help.name: menu-inspect
help.text:
agenterm-cu menu-inspect    (also: menu inspect)
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  menu inspect --window HANDLE [--depth N] [--max-nodes N] [--title T [--exact]]
               [--enabled true|false] [--offset N] [--max N]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --depth N                     0 = bar items, default 1, at most 8
  --max-nodes N                 node budget 1..5000
  --title T                     title filter (substring; --exact for equality)
  --exact                       match --title exactly
  --enabled true|false          keep only enabled / disabled items
  --offset N                    page start
  --max N                       page size

The application's menu bar read in the background (never opens a menu,
never activates): items with exact title paths, depth (0 = bar items,
default 1, <= 8), enabled / checked / has_submenu; node budget 1..5000;
counts visited / matched / returned / truncated.

help.name: get-text
help.text:
agenterm-cu get-text
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  get-text --window HANDLE [--name PAT] [--role ROLE]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role

One-shot independent AT-SPI Text.GetText on the unique showing named
node, or with no --name on the node carrying the AT-SPI focused state --
the same text authority wait --text-equals polls, without a timeout. Not
send-text / paste / copy matched.text, last_text_write_via, the WebKit eval
helper queued-job OK, or a tree snapshot text. Missing Text typed-fails
(a11y_text_unavailable). Never XTest / --coords / screenshot.

help.name: get-extents
help.text:
agenterm-cu get-extents
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  get-extents --window HANDLE --name PAT [--role ROLE]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role

Independent AT-SPI Component.GetExtents(Screen). Snapshot node.bounds do
not count. Empty extents typed-fail (a11y_extents_unavailable).

help.name: get-selection
help.text:
agenterm-cu get-selection
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  get-selection --window HANDLE --name PAT [--role ROLE]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role

Independent AT-SPI Text.GetNSelections + GetSelection(0). Not the select
reply payload. Missing Text typed-fails (a11y_selection_unavailable). n=0
is empty success.

help.name: get-caret
help.text:
agenterm-cu get-caret
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  get-caret --window HANDLE --name PAT [--role ROLE]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role

Independent AT-SPI Text.CaretOffset / GetCaretOffset. Not the set-caret
reply payload. Missing Text typed-fails (a11y_caret_unavailable).

help.name: wait
help.text:
agenterm-cu wait
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  wait --timeout-ms MS (--window-count-gte N | --window-title-contains PAT | --focused-handle HANDLE
                        | --window HANDLE --expect JSON
                        | --node-name-contains PAT [--node-role ROLE] [--window HANDLE]
                        | --text-equals TEXT --name PAT [--role ROLE] --window HANDLE
                        | --text-contains SUB --name PAT [--role ROLE] --window HANDLE) [-- TEXT]

arguments:
  --timeout-ms MS               deadline (default 5000); timeout is typed with the last observation
  --window-count-gte N          at least N top-level windows
  --window-title-contains PAT   some window title contains PAT
  --focused-handle HANDLE       that window holds focus
  --expect JSON                 same matcher as verify; polls until every item is met
  --node-name-contains PAT      a showing node's name contains PAT (--node-role narrows)
  --text-equals TEXT            independent Text.GetText on --name equals TEXT
  --text-contains SUB           independent Text.GetText on --name contains SUB
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)

--window HANDLE --expect JSON uses the same matcher as verify: polls
until every item is met, ambiguity / unobservable state fail at once,
timeout is typed with the last observation.
--text-equals / --node-text-equals and --text-contains / --node-text-contains
poll AT-SPI Text.GetText on the unique showing named node until that
independent text equals TEXT or contains SUB. send-text / paste / copy
matched.text, last_text_write_via, and the WebKit eval helper's queued-job
OK are not this condition. Timeout is typed ("timeout") and reports the
last GetText. Never screenshot / XTest / --coords. `--` ends flag parsing.

help.name: screenshot
help.text:
agenterm-cu screenshot    (also: shot)
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  screenshot [--out PATH | PATH] [--window HANDLE]

arguments:
  --out PATH                    PNG path (default: a temp file named by pid)
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)

Last resort, never the primary observation: the a11y verbs are. --window
is never a positional path. `shot` is the MCU spelling.

help.name: device-screenshot
help.text:
agenterm-cu device-screenshot
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  device-screenshot --list
  device-screenshot --out PATH [--device NAME|UID] [--timeout-ms N]

arguments:
  --list                        inventory sources plus host Camera authorization and usbmux evidence
  --out PATH                    new PNG path; existing destinations are never overwritten
  --device NAME|UID             exact published source name or uid (optional for a sole source)
  --timeout-ms N                first-frame deadline, 1..120000 (default 10000)

The host capture inventory and usbmux pairing are independent evidence. An
empty source list never proves the phone is locked or untrusted. Camera TCC
denial or undecided consent is reported as a host error; an authorized host
with no DAL source is device_source_not_published. Frame bytes are never
printed, and a successful capture atomically creates a new output path. This
uses Camera permission, not Screen Recording.

help.name: zoom
help.text:
agenterm-cu zoom
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  zoom --window HANDLE --region X,Y,W,H --out PATH [--replace] [--pad N]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --region X,Y,W,H              screen rectangle to crop (the space node bounds use)
  --out PATH                    PNG path
  --replace                     overwrite an existing file
  --pad N                       pixels of context kept around the region (default 8, at most 512)

Crops one region out of the window's own capture, so a caller can look
at a detail without a full-screen image. --region is in screen
coordinates -- the same space node bounds and query --within use -- so a
node's bounds can be passed straight in.

A region that does not intersect the window is typed
"region_outside_window" and NO file is written; a region that straddles
an edge is clipped to the window. --pad adds context around a region that
already intersects; it never rescues one that misses.

The crop is a clip of the window capture, never a screen grab: the reply
reports the capture size and the point -> pixel scale it applied (a
Retina window is captured at 2x, and the region is scaled into that
space). Still the last resort, like `screenshot`: the a11y verbs are the
primary observation.

help.name: pointer-position
help.text:
agenterm-cu pointer-position    (also: cursor)
  scope: observe    family: Accessibility: observe

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  pointer-position
  cursor                                              (alias)

Observes absolute screen coordinates without injecting any pointer event
(macOS: a read-only CGEvent sample; the journey reads it around every
click / close to prove the real pointer stayed put). `cursor` is the MCU
spelling.

help.name: invoke
help.text:
agenterm-cu invoke
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  invoke --window HANDLE (--node PATH | --index N | --name PAT [--role ROLE] | --identifier ID
                          | --focused [--role ROLE] | --selector PATH)
         <press | set-value TEXT | select-option NAME | set-checked true|false
          | set-expanded true|false | increment | decrement | scroll-to
          | set-selection START:LENGTH>

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --node PATH                   node path id from tree / query
  --index N                     flat index from tree --flat
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role
  --identifier ID               accessibility identifier
  --focused                     the application's own focused control (combine only with --role)
  --selector PATH               MCU selector path (not with --node/--index/--name/--identifier)
  <action> [VALUE]              exactly one action after the flags, at most one VALUE

One semantic a11y action; never activates or raises the window. Two
showing matches -> "ambiguous", none -> "a11y_node_not_found", an action
the node does not offer -> "unsupported". set-checked / set-expanded are
desired states (already there = verified no-op). The reply carries verified
true|false with the reason and a receipt (target, node, action, before /
after state). --focused acts on the application's own focused control (what
`focused` reports), bound by id / role / identifier in the same tree read;
--role narrows it ("unverified" when the focused control has another role).

help.name: menu-invoke
help.text:
agenterm-cu menu-invoke    (also: menu invoke)
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  menu invoke --window HANDLE --path 'Menu/Item' | '["Menu","Item"]'

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --path PATH                   'Menu/Item' or a JSON array of exact titles

Press one menu item by exact path in the background; every segment must
be exactly one enabled item before anything is pressed
("a11y_menu_item_not_found" / "..._ambiguous" / "..._disabled"), the last
must be a leaf ("..._not_leaf"), a bare menu is "invalid_input"; verified
by mark read-back / tree diff.

help.name: click
help.text:
agenterm-cu click    (also: dclick, rclick)
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  click (--window HANDLE --node ID | --window HANDLE --name PAT [--role ROLE] | --coords X,Y --degraded)
        [--button left|right|middle] [--clicks N]
  dclick ...                                          (alias of click --clicks 2)
  rclick ...                                          (alias of click --button right)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --to HANDLE                   MCU spelling of --window (not both; --to desktop is not mapped)
  --node ID                     node path id
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role
  --coords X,Y                  screen coordinates; requires --degraded
  --degraded                    admit the coordinate fallback
  --button left|right|middle    pointer button (default left)
  --clicks N                    click count (default 1)

--name reuses wait NodeNameContains matching, then the --node AT-SPI path.
`dclick` is click --clicks 2 and `rclick` is click --button right (MCU
spellings).

help.name: drag
help.text:
agenterm-cu drag
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  drag --window HANDLE --from X,Y --to X,Y [--button left|right|middle] [--steps N] [--degraded]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --from X,Y                    screen point of the press; must be inside the window
  --to X,Y                      screen point of the release
  --button left|right|middle    pointer button (default left)
  --steps N                     intermediate moves between press and release (default 12, at most 64)
  --degraded                    admit the path that moves the user's real pointer

One press, a bounded series of moves and one release, delivered as one
gesture. There is no semantic a11y path for a drag, so this is the
pointer, and the reply always says WHICH path ran (`path`) plus whether a
window-local one existed (window_local_available).

macOS has no window-local pointer injection at all: mouse events posted
to a pid arrive with no window for AppKit to route them through, so the
only working path is the global one that MOVES THE USER'S REAL CURSOR.
That makes --degraded a required opt-in there, exactly as for
click --coords; without it the verb refuses and names the path it would
have taken. Nothing is injected before that refusal.

--from must be inside the window (else typed "drag_outside_window",
nothing performed); --to may leave it, and to_inside_window says so. The
read-back is where the pointer ended up: the release happened at --to, so
pointer_after must equal it, and the receipt records pointer_before and
pointer_after either way. tree_changed reports whether the window's tree
moved, as supporting evidence.

help.name: focus
help.text:
agenterm-cu focus
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  focus [--window HANDLE] (--node ID | --window HANDLE --name PAT [--role ROLE])

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --node ID                     node path id
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role

Gives one node the accessibility focus through the a11y tree; never
raises or activates the window.

help.name: send-text
help.text:
agenterm-cu send-text    (also: type)
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  send-text [--window HANDLE [--name PAT [--role ROLE]]] [--allow-browser-chrome] [--] <text...>
  type ...                                            (alias)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role
  --allow-browser-chrome        with --window and no --name: write browser chrome (omnibox, toolbar, tab strip) instead of refusing
  --                            ends flag parsing so the text may start with a dash

--name writes via AT-SPI EditableText (SetTextContents / InsertText) or
AT-SPI Text + toolkit set-value when EditableText is absent (Chrome
renderer AX; WebKitGTK AT-SPI id + eval helper); a node with no writeable
text interface typed-fails (never XTest). --window without --name writes
that same path on the showing focused node (same innermost Text candidate
as get-text --window). Never XTest when --window is set. Without --window
stays the plain type-into-focused inject. `--` ends flag parsing. `type`
is the MCU spelling.
When the window's focused control is browser chrome (omnibox, toolbar, tab
strip) the write is refused with focused_node_is_browser_chrome unless
--allow-browser-chrome is passed; pass --name to address a page control
instead.

help.name: send-keys
help.text:
agenterm-cu send-keys    (also: key)
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  send-keys [--window HANDLE [--name PAT [--role ROLE]]] [--allow-browser-chrome] [--] <keys...>
  key ...                                             (alias)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role
  --allow-browser-chrome        with --window and no --name: write browser chrome (omnibox, toolbar, tab strip) instead of refusing
  --                            ends flag parsing so a chord may start with a dash

--name delivers AT-SPI Device/key events (DeviceEventListener
NotifyEvent); a node with no key interface typed-fails (never XTest).
--window without --name targets the showing focused node (same innermost
Text candidate as get-text --window). Prefers DeviceEventListener; plain
typeable text falls back to the AT-SPI EditableText/Text write path when
that interface is absent (con Command; Chrome; Reasonix). Never XTest when
--window is set. Without --window, the OS only acknowledges global focused
injection: the reply deliberately says performed=true, verified=false and
delivered=false because there is no target read-back. Use an exact window/node
semantic action when delivery proof matters; JSON ok alone is not proof. `--`
ends flag parsing. e.g. ctrl+c / enter / k. `key` is the MCU spelling.
When the window's focused control is browser chrome (omnibox, toolbar, tab
strip) the write is refused with focused_node_is_browser_chrome unless
--allow-browser-chrome is passed; pass --name to address a page control
instead.

help.name: scroll
help.text:
agenterm-cu scroll
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  scroll --window HANDLE --name PAT [--role ROLE]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role

help.name: select
help.text:
agenterm-cu select
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  select --window HANDLE --name PAT --start N --end M [--role ROLE]

arguments:

  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --start N                     selection start offset
  --end M                       selection end offset
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role

addressing=accessibility-tree via=set-selection. Missing Text /
UnknownMethod typed-fails (a11y_selection_unavailable). SetSelection false

help.name: set-caret

agenterm-cu set-caret
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate
