help.name: pointer-move
help.text:
agenterm-cu pointer-move    (also: move)
  scope: actuate    family: Accessibility: actuate

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  pointer-move --to desktop --x X --y Y
  move ...                                            (alias)

arguments:
  --to desktop                  explicit global coordinates; --to <handle> answers typed unsupported
  --x X                         signed 32-bit screen x
  --y Y                         signed 32-bit screen y

Moves to absolute screen coordinates without any press / release / click
/ drag / wheel side effect. Window-local pointer is not mapped: use click
--window. `move` is the MCU spelling.

help.name: page-js
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-js    (also: page read)
  scope: observe    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  page-js [--window HANDLE] --expression EXPR [--port N | --pid PID]
          [--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB]
  page read --js EXPR [...]                           (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --expression EXPR             JavaScript expression (MCU: --js)
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description

Second knife: CDP Runtime.evaluate on 127.0.0.1:N (default 9222).
MAIN-world Function constructor is refused. No listener -> typed
unsupported with backend debugger-runtime-evaluate. One selector picks the
page target (tab): exact id, a case-insensitive substring of its URL/title,
or `--match` across title + URL + description. No match -> "cdp_target_not_found", more than one ->
"cdp_target_ambiguous" (candidates in error.detail). None keeps the first
page. The chosen id/url/title is echoed; a background tab is evaluated in
place, never selected or raised. Chrome / Brave must be started with
--remote-debugging-port=9222 for every CDP path; that port answers any
local process, so open it only while needed.

help.name: page-targets
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-targets    (also: page targets)
  scope: observe    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  page-targets [--port N | --pid PID] [--browser-profile SUB]
  page targets [--port N | --pid PID] [--browser-profile SUB]     (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --browser-profile SUB         case-insensitive substring of the window's browser_profile (Chromium profile name)

The CDP /json inventory: id, url, title, type, attached, websocket
(offered or not). Pick a --target-id here. No listener -> typed
unsupported. `--pid` is exclusive with `--port` and performs an identity-bound
exact-process discovery without port scanning or command-line publication.
Chrome / Brave must be started with
--remote-debugging-port=9222 for every CDP path; that port answers any
local process, so open it only while needed.

--browser-profile SUB joins the inventory to one profile: only targets
whose title equals (exactly) a tab title of a window whose
browser_profile contains SUB are returned, each with profile_match:
"title", window and browser_profile. This is a heuristic and the reply
says so: one CDP port serves every profile of an instance and a target
carries no profile field, so a title shared across profiles matches each
of them and a differently spelled strip title (memory-saver suffix,
unset document title) is left out. No such window ->
browser_window_not_found before any socket is opened.

help.name: page-text
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-text    (also: page text)
  scope: observe    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  page-text --window HANDLE [--max-bytes N] [--within X,Y,W,H] [--depth N] [--max-nodes N]
  page-text [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB) [--max-bytes N]
  page text ...  |  page read [...]                   (MCU spellings)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --max-bytes N                 text budget (default 16 KiB, max 1 MiB)
  --within X,Y,W,H              a11y only: screen rectangle the rows must intersect
  --depth N                     a11y only: walk depth (default 64)
  --max-nodes N                 a11y only: walk budget (default 6000)
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description

The page's visible text in reading order as compact rows {id, role,
text} (+ name when it differs, focused, editable / actionable) -- never a
screenshot. Two backends, one row shape, so the caller does not care
which answered:

--window HANDLE reads the a11y tree of that window (rows carry bounds;
backend ax / uia / at-spi2). On macOS Chromium only the active tab has a
web-area there, so a background tab needs `tab select` first. Web
static-text keeps its words in AXValue; a link / button is one row (its
inner text merged). A container role is never a row of its own even when
the backend hands back its whole concatenated text (Windows UIA reports a
Chromium web root as Document, whose TextPattern is the entire page): the
rows are the nodes inside it, each with an id worth clicking. Then invoke
--node / click --node. Walk budget defaults depth 64 / 6000 nodes because
the platform's 1000-node breadth-first budget is spent on browser chrome
before web content.

--target-id | --target-url | --target-title | --match [--port N] reads the CDP page
target instead (backend "cdp", via Accessibility.getFullAXTree; fallback
Runtime.evaluate innerText walk when that domain is unavailable). This
reaches a background tab in a background window and changes nothing
about which tab or window is active (focus_changed: false). Row `id` /
`node` is then the backend DOM node id that page click --node / page
fill --node take; no bounds (page find carries the box). One backend per
call. Default 16 KiB (max 1 MiB), truncated flag.

help.name: page-find
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-find    (also: page find)
  scope: observe    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  page-find [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB)
          (--selector CSS | --text SUB | --role R [--name SUB])
  page find ...                                       (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --selector CSS                CSS selector (DOM.querySelectorAll)
  --text SUB                    case-insensitive substring of the node's words (AX tree; lifted to the enclosing button / link)
  --role R                      AX role (button, link, textbox, StaticText, ...; case-insensitive)
  --name SUB                    with --role: case-insensitive substring of the accessible name

The matching nodes of one CDP page target (a background tab in a
background window included; nothing is activated): {node, path, tag,
role, name, text, value, editable, ax_id, box}. --selector runs
DOM.querySelectorAll; --text and --role filter Accessibility.getFullAXTree
(a text hit inside a button / link is lifted to that control, so the
click lands on it). `node` is the backend DOM node id the actuators take
(page click --node / page fill --node); `box` is the layout box in
viewport CSS px. Zero matches -> cdp_node_not_found; more than 20 are
counted (total) and cut (truncated). The target selector rules are those
of page-js (cdp_target_not_found / cdp_target_ambiguous).

help.name: page-click
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-click    (also: page click)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  page-click [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB)
          ((--selector CSS | --text SUB | --node ID) | --x X --y Y) [--button left|right|middle] [--clicks N]
  page click ...                                      (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --selector CSS                CSS selector (DOM.querySelectorAll)
  --text SUB                    case-insensitive substring of the node's words (AX tree; lifted to the enclosing button / link)
  --node ID                     backend DOM node id from page-find / page-text rows
  --x X                         viewport CSS x coordinate (pixel compatibility path)
  --y Y                         viewport CSS y coordinate (pixel compatibility path)
  --button B                    left (default) | right | middle
  --clicks N                    1 (default) ..= 3 press / release pairs

Either resolves exactly one node (zero -> cdp_node_not_found, more ->
cdp_node_ambiguous with candidates; narrow the selector or pass --node), or freezes one
explicit --x/--y viewport point. The node path scrolls into view and takes the box centre.
The point path proves a rendered hit exists, then verifies trusted mousedown/up events at
the frozen point and always attempts release after a successful press. Both dispatch
Input.dispatchMouseEvent on that page target. The tab is not selected and the window is not raised
(focus_changed: false); focus emulation is switched on for the click and
off after so an unfocused page handles it normally. A node without a
layout box -> cdp_node_not_visible, nothing dispatched. Verified by
Node clicks are verified by reading the document and node back; point clicks use the trusted
event sequence so a legitimate no-op target can still be verified. Receipt reserved before
the dispatch, completed after.

help.name: page-download
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-download    (also: page download)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  page-download [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB)
          (--selector CSS | --text SUB | --node ID) --download-dir PATH [--wait-ms N]
  page download ...                                   (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --selector CSS                CSS selector for the download control
  --text SUB                    case-insensitive words of the download control
  --node ID                     backend DOM node id from page-find / page-text rows
  --download-dir PATH           existing absolute directory on the browser host
  --wait-ms N                   download start and completion deadline, 1..=300000

Resolves exactly one background-page control, takes the cross-process lock
for that CDP endpoint, then sets Browser.setDownloadBehavior to allowAndName
with download events enabled before dispatching the click. Completion is a
matching Browser.downloadWillBegin plus Browser.downloadProgress state=completed
and a final regular non-symlink file that stat resolves as download-dir/GUID.
The result includes guid, suggested filename, final path, state and decimal byte
counts; file contents are never opened or copied to stdout. The tab is not selected
and the browser window is not raised (focus_changed: false). Every exit attempts
to restore the browser download policy. A held endpoint lock, rejected policy,
canceled transfer, absent start event, deadline, or missing final file fails typed
as cdp_download_busy / _blocked / _canceled / _not_started / _timeout /
_file_missing instead of treating the click acknowledgement as success.

help.name: page-hover
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-hover    (also: page hover)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  page-hover [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB) --x X --y Y
  page hover ...                                      (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --x X                         viewport CSS x coordinate
  --y Y                         viewport CSS y coordinate

Dispatches mouseMoved to one CDP page target without selecting
the tab or raising the window. Coordinates are finite non-negative viewport
CSS pixels. performed means Chromium accepted the event; verified compares
the trusted mousemove target and coordinates with elementFromPoint. The
deepest :hover node is auxiliary because headless/background Chromium may
not maintain it. A point outside
rendered page content is cdp_point_not_found. Receipt reserved before the
dispatch and completed after read-back.

help.name: page-scroll
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-scroll    (also: page scroll)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  page-scroll [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB) --x X --y Y [--dx DX] [--dy DY]
  page scroll ...                                     (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --x X                         viewport CSS x coordinate
  --y Y                         viewport CSS y coordinate
  --dx DX                       horizontal wheel delta (default 0)
  --dy DY                       vertical wheel delta (default 120)

Dispatches mouseWheel at one viewport point without selecting
the tab or raising the window. The nearest scrollable container is captured
before dispatch and its exact offsets are read back afterwards. performed
means Chromium accepted the wheel event; verified requires left or top to
change. A boundary that cannot move is honestly performed but unverified
(no_observable_scroll_change). Receipt reserved before dispatch.

help.name: page-files
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-files    (also: page files)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  page-files [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB)
          (--selector CSS | --node ID) FILE...
  page files [--node] ID FILE...                     (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --selector CSS                CSS selector (DOM.querySelectorAll)
  --node ID                     backend DOM node id from page-find / page-text rows
  FILE...                       1..=16 absolute regular non-symlink files on the browser host

Resolves exactly one enabled input[type=file], refuses more
than one file unless the control has `multiple`, validates bounded regular
non-symlink local files, then calls DOM.setFileInputFiles on the selected CDP
target. FileList basename and size are read back exactly. Replies and persistent
receipts never contain local paths. The tab/window stays backgrounded and no
native file-picker is opened.

help.name: page-drag
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-drag    (also: page drag)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  page-drag [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB) --x1 X --y1 Y --x2 X --y2 Y
  page drag X1 Y1 X2 Y2 ...                         (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --x1 X                        start viewport CSS x
  --y1 Y                        start viewport CSS y
  --x2 X                        end viewport CSS x
  --y2 Y                        end viewport CSS y

Moves to the start, presses left, moves to the end while
held, and always attempts release after a successful press. The selected tab
is not activated. performed requires all four CDP dispatches; verified requires
the target page to observe a trusted mousedown, held mousemove and mouseup at
the frozen endpoints. A zero-distance drag is rejected before any effect.

help.name: page-dialog
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-dialog    (also: page dialog)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  page-dialog [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB) [--dismiss] [--text TEXT] [--wait-ms N]
  page dialog ...                                     (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --dismiss                     dismiss instead of accept
  --text TEXT                   prompt response (accept only; redacted from receipt)
  --wait-ms N                   dialog-opening deadline, 1..=30000 (default 3000)

Enables Page events, waits for a real
Page.javascriptDialogOpening, reserves the receipt, then calls
Page.handleJavaScriptDialog and verifies Page.javascriptDialogClosed. A missing
dialog is cdp_dialog_not_open and performs nothing. Dialog message, default
prompt, supplied response and returned userInput are represented only by byte
counts in persistent/public evidence.

help.name: page-fill
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-fill    (also: page fill)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  page-fill [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB)
          (--selector CSS | --node ID) --text TEXT [--clear] [--submit]
  page fill ...                                       (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --selector CSS                CSS selector (DOM.querySelectorAll)
  --node ID                     backend DOM node id from page-find / page-text rows
  --text TEXT                   what to insert (<= 64 KiB; empty only with --clear)
  --clear                       select everything first so the text replaces the field
  --submit                      then dispatch Enter key down / up

Resolves exactly one editable node (an enabled input / textarea /
contenteditable; anything else -> cdp_node_not_editable, nothing
written), DOM.focus, optional select-all (--clear), Input.insertText,
then reads .value (or the text content) back; --submit dispatches Enter
key events afterwards and echoes the document state. Focus emulation is
switched on for the write and off after, so a background tab accepts it
without being brought forward (focus_changed: false). Verified when the
read-back equals TEXT (--clear) or grew by exactly TEXT (append at the
caret); a mismatch is performed but unverified (value_mismatch), for a
page that rewrites its own field. Receipt reserved before the write,
        completed after.

help.name: page-type
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-type    (also: page type)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  page-type [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB) --text TEXT
  page type TEXT ...                                  (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --text TEXT                   1..=64 KiB inserted at the page's existing editable focus

Freezes the page's already-focused input, textarea or
contenteditable before reserving a receipt; missing or non-editable focus performs
nothing. Input.insertText then writes without selecting the tab or raising its window.
Verification requires the same focused-element path and exact value-length growth
containing the inserted text. Text and field values never enter public or persistent
evidence; only byte counts, element identity and the typed verdict do.

help.name: page-nav
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-nav    (also: page nav)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  page-nav [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB) --url URL [--wait-ms N]
  page nav ...                                        (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --url URL                     where to go (needs a scheme: https:, data:, file:, about:)
  --wait-ms N                   how long to wait for Page.loadEventFired (default 10000, max 120000)

Page.navigate on that page target -- a background tab stays a
background tab, the window is not raised (focus_changed: false) -- then
waits up to --wait-ms for Page.loadEventFired. A navigation Chromium
refuses at once (errorText, e.g. a DNS failure) -> cdp_navigation_failed.
Verified when the load event fired (or readyState reads complete on the
new url); a timeout is performed but unverified (load_timeout) with the
url / title read so far. Reply: final_url, final_title, waited_ms,
receipt.

help.name: page-screenshot
help.text:
agenterm-cu page-screenshot    (also: page screenshot)
  scope: observe    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  page-screenshot [--port N | --pid PID] (--target-id ID | --target-url SUB | --target-title SUB | --match SUB) --out PATH [--replace] [--activate]
  page screenshot ...                                 (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --port N                      CDP listener port on 127.0.0.1 (default 9222)
  --pid PID                     browser process whose explicit --remote-debugging-port is used (exclusive with --port)
  --target-id ID                exact CDP target id (from page-targets)
  --target-url SUB              case-insensitive url substring of the page target
  --target-title SUB            case-insensitive title substring of the page target
  --match SUB                   case-insensitive substring across target title, URL and description
  --out PATH                    where the PNG is written (refuses an existing file without --replace)
  --replace                     overwrite --out
  --activate                    actuate: Page.bringToFront first (the only CDP verb that changes the active tab)

Page.captureScreenshot (PNG) of that page target, written to --out with
its sha256 in the reply. Chromium does not paint a tab that is not
visible, so a background or occluded tab may answer
cdp_screenshot_unavailable; this verb never activates the tab to get a
picture. --activate is the one explicit opt-in: it runs Page.bringToFront
first, needs the actuate grant, writes a receipt, and replies
focus_changed: true. Prefer page text / page find, which need no pixels.

help.name: tab-list
help.text:
agenterm-cu tab-list    (also: tab list)
  scope: observe    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  tab-list --window HANDLE
  tab list --window HANDLE                            (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)

The browser tab strip through the a11y tree: index, title, selected per
tab. The strip is read on every backend, whatever it calls the roles:
macOS AX tab-group / radio-button, AT-SPI2 and UIA both "page tab list" /
"page tab" (roles are compared on their alphanumeric core, so separator
and AX-prefix spellings all match). A background tab's content is never in
the tree -- only its row is; use tab select, or the CDP page verbs.

Evidence: macOS is proven on a real Brave instance
(scripts/cu-brave-live-smoke.sh). Linux and Windows are code-complete with
no live run yet; scripts/cu-linux-smoke.sh and
scripts/qjs/cu-windows-browser-smoke.qjs carry the journey and exit with a
typed SKIP until a host with a Chromium-family browser runs them.

help.name: tab-select
help.text:
agenterm-cu tab-select    (also: tab select)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  tab-select --window HANDLE (--title SUB | --index N)
  tab select ...                                      (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --title SUB                   tab title substring (not with --index)
  --index N                     tab index from tab-list (not with --title)

Presses one tab-strip row in the background so it becomes the window's
active tab; never raises or activates the window. No such tab ->
"a11y_tab_not_found", two title hits -> "a11y_tab_ambiguous"; verified by
reading selected back (already selected = verified no-op). The a11y
fallback when no CDP port is open.

help.name: tab-close
help.text:
agenterm-cu tab-close    (also: tab close)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  tab-close --window HANDLE (--title T --exact | --index N) --expect gone [--port N]
  tab close ...                                       (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --title T                     the tab's exact title (from tab-list); needs --exact
  --index N                     the tab's strip index from tab-list (0-based); the exact selector for same-title duplicates
  --exact                       required with --title: the title is matched exactly, never as a substring
  --expect gone                 checkable postcondition: one fewer strip row with that title reads back
  --port N                      CDP port: close by Target.closeTarget when the title names exactly one page target of the instance; else the a11y path

Destructive, so gated like close: --window H plus --title T --exact
(exact, case-sensitive title equality; no match -> a11y_tab_not_found,
two -> a11y_tab_ambiguous, name one with --index) or --index N (tab-list
order) names the tab, the strip snapshot is written to the receipt
before anything is pressed, and --expect gone is the postcondition read
back from the tab strip (one fewer row with that title, up to 2.5 s).
Any missing part -> refused (destructive_gate) with nothing performed.
The press goes to the tab row's own close button (the button child of
the Chromium tab radio-button). macOS Chromium exposes that button on
the selected (or hovered) tab only, so a background tab is selected
first in the same window (never raising it), closed, and the previously
selected tab is pressed again; the reply says selection_restored
true|false and select_first. With --port N and a listener, a title that
names exactly one page target of the whole instance is closed by
Target.closeTarget instead (via cdp-close-target, no selection change);
no listener, no such target, or two targets fall back to the a11y path
(cdp_fallback says why). A keyboard shortcut is never substituted.
Reply: performed, verified, via, before / after strip rows, receipt.

help.name: browser-profiles
help.text:
agenterm-cu browser-profiles    (also: browser profiles)
  scope: observe    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  browser-profiles [--app SUB]
  browser profiles [--app SUB]                        (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --app SUB                     Brave Origin | Brave Browser | Google Chrome (substring; default: the one running)

Reads the application's Chromium `Local State` (profile.info_cache:
directory -> display name; profile.last_used) and joins each profile to
the inventory windows whose browser_profile equals its name. Rows: {name,
directory, last_used, windows: [handles]}; browser windows whose profile
name is not in Local State are listed under unlisted_windows. --app is a
catalog substring (Brave Origin -> ~/Library/Application
Support/BraveSoftware/Brave-Origin, Brave Browser -> .../Brave-Browser,
Google Chrome -> .../Google/Chrome; Linux under ~/.config); omitted, the
one running catalog application is used (none -> browser_app_not_found,
several -> browser_app_ambiguous). Any other application -> typed
unsupported. Never touches the browser.

help.name: browser-open
help.text:
agenterm-cu browser-open    (also: browser open)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  browser-open --profile NAME [--url URL] [--app SUB] [--timeout-ms N]
  browser open ...                                    (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --profile NAME                profile name from browser-profiles (exact, else unique case-insensitive substring)
  --url URL                     open this URL in the profile (a tab of its window when it has one)
  --app SUB                     Brave Origin | Brave Browser | Google Chrome (substring; default: the one running)
  --timeout-ms N                how long to wait for the window (default 8000, max 120000)

Resolves NAME to its profile directory (exact name first, then a unique
case-insensitive substring; browser_profile_not_found /
browser_profile_ambiguous carry the candidates) and runs macOS `open -na
<app> --args --profile-directory=<dir> [URL]`: the Chromium process
singleton hands that command line to the running instance, which opens a
window of the profile (or, with a URL, a tab in the profile's existing
window) and the user's browser is never quit or restarted. Then polls the
window inventory (default 8000 ms) until a window with that
browser_profile appears that was not in the before snapshot, or -- when
the profile already had a window and a URL was given -- until that
window's title changes. Reply: {handle, browser_profile, title, created,
tab_index, tab_title, tabs: {before, after}} -- the new tab is the
selected row the window's strip gained (diffed against the strip read
before the launch; null when none can be told apart) -- plus the receipt
(reserved before `open`, completed / failed after the read-back); timeout
-> browser_window_not_found. `open` activates the browser, so this is
actuation; nothing here needs a CDP port. Without --url the profile's own
last session is restored: after a browser restart only the last-used
profile comes back by itself, and `browser open --profile X` is how the
other profiles' windows are brought back.

help.name: browser-session-start
help.text:
agenterm-cu browser-session-start    (also: browser session-start)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage:
  browser-session-start NAME --browser PATH [--ready-timeout-ms N] [--ttl-ms N]

Starts one named browser automation session with an exact browser executable path. Readiness is bounded to 1000..=60000 ms (default 15000); lifetime is bounded to 1000..=86400000 ms (default 3600000).

help.name: browser-session-list
help.text:
agenterm-cu browser-session-list    (also: browser session-list)
  scope: observe    family: Browser page & tabs

usage:
  browser-session-list

Lists the browser automation sessions owned by this runtime.

help.name: browser-session-status
help.text:
agenterm-cu browser-session-status    (also: browser session-status)
  scope: observe    family: Browser page & tabs

usage:
  browser-session-status NAME

Observes one named browser automation session.

help.name: browser-session-stop
help.text:
agenterm-cu browser-session-stop    (also: browser session-stop)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage:
  browser-session-stop NAME --expect stopped [--timeout-ms N]

Stops one named browser automation session and requires the literal stopped postcondition. The deadline is 1000..=60000 ms (default 15000).

help.name: browser-session-remove
help.text:
agenterm-cu browser-session-remove    (also: browser session-remove)
  scope: actuate    family: Browser page & tabs

usage:
  browser-session-remove NAME --expect stopped|failed

Removes one named browser automation session only when its recorded terminal state exactly matches the caller's literal expectation and both recorded processes are independently verified absent.

help.name: page
help.text:
agenterm-cu page
  scope: observe    family: Browser page & tabs

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  page read [--js EXPR] | page targets | page text | page find | page click | page download | page hover | page scroll | page drag | page dialog | page files | page fill | page nav | page screenshot
  page [<other>]                                      (typed unsupported)

MCU page: `page read --js` -> page-js, `page read` (no --js) -> the CDP
page-text, `page targets` -> page-targets, `page text` -> page-text (a11y
with --window, CDP with a target selector), and the CDP background-tab
verbs `page find` / `page click` / `page download` / `page hover` / `page scroll` / `page
drag` / `page dialog` / `page files` / `page fill` / `page nav` / `page screenshot` map to their typed CDP verbs. Any
other page sub-verb answers typed unsupported.

help.name: clipboard-read
help.text:
agenterm-cu clipboard-read    (also: clip, clipboard, clipboard read)
  scope: observe    family: Clipboard

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  clipboard-read [--type T] [--max-bytes N] [--out PATH [--replace]]
  clipboard [read] [T] [...]                          (MCU spelling)
  clip                                                (text only)

arguments:
  --type T                      one native type name (positional T also accepted)
  --max-bytes N                 byte budget (default 1 MiB, max 16 MiB); requires --type
  --out PATH                    write the bytes (0600); requires --type
  --replace                     overwrite --out

No --type: Unicode text plus host type names. --type T: one native type
as bounded bytes (default 1 MiB, max 16 MiB), sha256, utf8 or base64.
--out writes the bytes (0600; --replace overwrites). Requires observe.
`clip` takes no arguments and reads text; `clipboard` with no sub-command
is clipboard-read.

help.name: clipboard-write
help.text:
agenterm-cu clipboard-write    (also: clipboard write)
  scope: actuate    family: Clipboard

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  clipboard-write --type T --path P
  clipboard write T P                                 (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --type T                      native type name
  --path P                      regular file (<= 16 MiB)

Publish one native type from a regular file (<= 16 MiB) and read it back
(actuate).

help.name: clipboard-write-file
help.text:
agenterm-cu clipboard-write-file    (also: clipboard write-file)
  scope: actuate    family: Clipboard

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  clipboard-write-file --path P
  clipboard write-file P                              (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --path P                      file to reference

Put a file reference on the clipboard (macOS POSIX file / Linux
text/uri-list / Windows CF_HDROP), not the file bytes (actuate).

help.name: clipboard-clear
help.text:
agenterm-cu clipboard-clear    (also: clipboard clear)
  scope: actuate    family: Clipboard

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  clipboard-clear [--apply]
  clipboard clear [--apply]                           (MCU spelling)

arguments:
  --apply                       perform it; without --apply the reply is planned only

Empty the clipboard. Without --apply this is planned and performs nothing
(actuate).

help.name: copy
help.text:
agenterm-cu copy
  scope: actuate    family: Clipboard

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  copy --window HANDLE [--name PAT [--role ROLE]]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role

Copies AT-SPI Text.GetText onto the native clipboard (Linux X11:
SetSelectionOwner, not xclip). addressing=accessibility-tree via=gettext.
--name targets the unique showing named node. --window without --name
copies that same path on the showing focused node (same innermost Text
candidate as get-text --window; con Command via=gettext on a second con
that never steals the resident control socket; Chrome GetTextField;
Reasonix Message Reasonix... under scripts/reasonix-desktop-a11y.sh). Never
XTest when --window is set. A node with no Text interface typed-fails
(never XTest / --coords / screenshot). Close the circuit with paste
--window (no --text / no --name) then get-text --window / wait
--text-equals; copy matched.text does not count.

help.name: paste
help.text:
agenterm-cu paste
  scope: actuate    family: Clipboard

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  paste --window HANDLE [--name PAT [--role ROLE]] [--allow-browser-chrome] [--text TEXT] [-- TEXT]

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --name PAT                    unique showing node whose name contains PAT (wait matching)
  --role ROLE                   narrow --name to one role
  --allow-browser-chrome        with --window and no --name: write browser chrome (omnibox, toolbar, tab strip) instead of refusing
  --text TEXT                   seed the clipboard first (the write still reads the clipboard)
  --                            ends flag parsing so --text may start with a dash

Writes clipboard text via native AT-SPI EditableText / Text
(addressing=accessibility-tree). --text only seeds the clipboard; the field
write always reads the clipboard. --name targets the unique showing named
field. --window without --name writes that same path on the showing
focused node (same innermost Text candidate as get-text --window; con
Command via=editable-text on a second con that never steals the resident
control socket; Chrome GetTextField; Reasonix Message Reasonix...). Never
XTest when --window is set. A node with no writeable text interface
typed-fails (never XTest / --coords / screenshot). Close the circuit with
get-text --window / wait --text-equals; paste matched.text does not count.
`--` ends flag parsing.
When the window's focused control is browser chrome (omnibox, toolbar, tab
strip) the write is refused with focused_node_is_browser_chrome unless
--allow-browser-chrome is passed; pass --name to address a page control
instead.

help.name: window-place
help.text:
agenterm-cu window-place
  scope: actuate    family: Window placement

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  window-place --action <id> [--window HANDLE] [--x X --y Y --width W --height H]
      ids: center|fullscreen|left-half|right-half|top-half|bottom-half
           upper-left|lower-left|upper-right|lower-right
           next-third|previous-third|next-display|previous-display
           larger|smaller|undo|redo|move|resize|frame  (or SpectacleWindowAction* constants)

arguments:
  --action ID                   placement action id (positional ID also accepted)
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --x/--y/--width/--height N    the rect for --action frame; all four or none

The product placement catalog shared with the desktop-host menu and
global shortcuts. `frame`, `movewin`, `resize` and `maximize` are the MCU
shorthands and answer as window-place.

help.name: frame
help.text:
agenterm-cu frame
  scope: actuate    family: Window placement    reply.command: window-place

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  frame HANDLE|--window H --x X --y Y --width W --height H   (or HANDLE X Y W H)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --x/--y/--width/--height N    the requested rect (positional X Y W H also accepted)

Alias of window-place --action frame. The reply's command is
window-place.

help.name: movewin
help.text:
agenterm-cu movewin
  scope: actuate    family: Window placement    reply.command: window-place

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  movewin HANDLE|--window H --x X --y Y   (or HANDLE X Y)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --x/--y N                     new origin (positional X Y also accepted)

Alias of window-place move; keeps the current size. The reply's command
is window-place.

help.name: resize
help.text:
agenterm-cu resize
  scope: actuate    family: Window placement    reply.command: window-place

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  resize HANDLE|--window H --width W --height H   (or HANDLE W H)

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --width/--height N            new size (positional W H also accepted)

Alias of window-place resize; keeps the current origin. The reply's
command is window-place.

help.name: maximize
help.text:
agenterm-cu maximize
  scope: actuate    family: Window placement    reply.command: window-place

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  maximize HANDLE|--window H

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)

Alias of window-place --action fullscreen. The reply's command is
window-place.

help.name: orderwin
help.text:
agenterm-cu orderwin
  scope: actuate    family: Window placement

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  orderwin --window HANDLE --relation above|below --relative HANDLE

arguments:
  --window HANDLE               window handle from `windows` (numeric or App#N)
  --relation above|below        above raises --window; below raises --relative
  --relative HANDLE             the other window

MCU relative z-order: above raises --window, below raises --relative,
then reads the order back and answers from what it read:
window_order_not_applied when the raise did not take. Linux raises with
the EWMH _NET_RESTACK_WINDOW (no focus change); macOS AXRaise cannot
reorder a background application's windows, so it refuses rather than
activating it.

help.name: exec
help.text:
agenterm-cu exec
  scope: none       family: Transports

usage:
  agenterm-cu exec [--grant observe,actuate] [--grant-id ID] [--grant-store PATH] --json '<command-json>'
  agenterm-cu exec [...] --json -  |  --json-stdin  |  -            (JSON command on stdin)

arguments:
  --json JSON|-                 the command payload, or - for stdin
  --json-stdin                  read the payload from stdin
  --grant S                     strict scopes (also --grant=S); CLI wins over AGENTERM_CU_GRANT
  --grant-id ID                 persisted grant selector (exclusive with every other source)
  --grant-store PATH            store override; valid only with --grant-id

Executes one Command serialized as JSON (the same shape `verbs --json`
consumers build). The ssh and vnc transports spawn `agenterm-cu --grant …
exec --json -` on the worker side; global flags may precede `exec`. The
command's own target and scope apply; grant sources never union.

help.name: grant
help.text:
agenterm-cu grant
  scope: none       family: Grants, host & help

usage:
  agenterm-cu grant create --target current --scopes S --ttl-ms N (--one-shot|--max-uses N) [--grant-store PATH]
  agenterm-cu grant list [--grant-store PATH]
  agenterm-cu grant revoke --grant-id ID [--grant-store PATH]

arguments:
  --scopes S                    observe, actuate or observe,actuate
  --ttl-ms N                    lifetime
  --one-shot                    single use
  --max-uses N                  bounded use count
  --grant-store PATH            explicit store (test / admin seam)

Grant management is local/current only. It refuses ambient
AGENTERM_CU_GRANT* and AGENTERM_CU_AUTH* selectors; --grant-store is an
explicit test/admin seam. A created grant is selected on later commands
with --grant-id ID, which is mutually exclusive with --grant and the
environment.

help.name: host
help.text:
agenterm-cu host    (also: hotkeys)
  scope: none       family: Grants, host & help

usage:
  agenterm-cu host
  agenterm-cu hotkeys                                             (compatibility alias)

Runs this binary as the resident desktop host: a status menu and global
shortcuts that route the placement catalog through the same Command ->
Executor chain as the CLI. `hotkeys` is the compatibility alias.

help.name: help
help.text:
agenterm-cu help
  scope: none       family: Grants, host & help

usage:
  agenterm-cu help [<verb> | ssh | vnc | rdp]
  agenterm-cu <verb> --help                                       (same as help <verb>)

With no argument: the grouped command list. With a verb (any spelling):
usage, arguments and the long reference for that verb. The topics ssh,
vnc and rdp describe the transports. An unknown name is a typed usage
error that lists near matches.

help.name: verbs
help.text:
agenterm-cu verbs
  scope: none       family: Grants, host & help

usage:
  agenterm-cu verbs [--json | --text]

arguments:
  --json                        JSON array (the default when stdout is not a terminal)
  --text                        aligned text table

Every row of the verb table: name, command, aliases, grant, family,
summary, usage and args. The JSON form is the machine-readable surface for
agents and generated docs; it is exactly what `--help` and `help <verb>`
render.

help.name: process-cwd
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-cwd    (also: process cwd)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  process-cwd --pid N
  process cwd PID

arguments:
  --pid N                       positive process id (or positional PID)

Reads the native working directory between two matching process-start
identity observations. This explicit command returns the path; persistent
evidence retains only its UTF-8 byte length and SHA-256. Linux uses procfs and
macOS uses libproc vnode data. Windows returns process_cwd_unsupported because
there is no stable public API; ACU does not read undocumented remote PEB layouts.
Exit, PID reuse, permission denial, unavailable cwd and invalid native data are
distinct typed failures.

help.name: privilege-plan
help.text:
agenterm-cu privilege-plan    (also: privilege plan)
  scope: observe    family: Privilege

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  privilege-plan process.set-priority PID|self NICE [--ttl-seconds N]
  privilege plan process.set-priority PID|self NICE [--ttl-seconds N]

arguments:
  process.set-priority           the closed operation in this first slice
  PID|self                       positive process id, or the planner process
  NICE                           requested Unix nice value in -20..=20
  --ttl-seconds N                approval lifetime, 1..=600 (default 120)

Observes the exact process start identity and current nice value twice, then
returns a canonical expiring plan with contract_digest and approval_digest.
It never changes priority, starts a broker, invokes a shell, or opens consent.
Windows returns privilege_operation_unsupported until a semantically equivalent
priority-class contract exists; it never pretends Unix nice is portable there.

help.name: process-set-state
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-set-state    (also: process set-state)
  scope: actuate    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant actuate):
  process-set-state --pid N --start-identity ID running|stopped [--timeout-ms N]
  process set-state PID running|stopped --start-identity ID [--timeout-ms N]

Opens one native process object, revalidates the supplied start identity, sends
SIGSTOP/SIGCONT through Linux pidfd or the macOS audit token, then reads the
scheduler state back before returning verified=true. It never reopens the PID as
effect authority. Windows returns process_state_unsupported rather than using
undocumented thread suspension. A no-op requested state is verified and reports
changed=false without reserving an effect receipt.

help.name: process-environment
help.text:
agenterm-cu process-environment    (also: process env)
  scope: observe    family: Processes

usage (after the global flags, e.g. agenterm-cu --target current --grant observe):
  process-environment --pid N [--prefix TEXT] [--offset N] [--limit N] [--values]
  process env PID [--prefix TEXT] [--offset N] [--limit N] [--values]

arguments:
  --pid N                       positive process id (or positional PID)
  --prefix TEXT                 filter names by UTF-8 byte prefix (max 256 bytes)
  --offset N                    first sorted matching entry (default 0)
  --limit N                     entries returned, 1..=5000 (default 256)
  --values                      explicitly include environment values

Reads the bounded native exec-time environment snapshot between two matching
process-start identity observations. This is not a promise to observe mutations
a process made after exec. Entries are split at the first equals sign, raw-byte
sorted, prefix-filtered, then paged; duplicates and empty values are preserved.
By default values are represented only by byte length and SHA-256. --values is
an explicit disclosure request. Non-UTF-8 bytes are never replaced lossily.
Linux uses /proc/PID/environ; macOS uses KERN_PROCARGS2 and typed-fails when the
kernel omits restricted data. Windows returns process_environment_unsupported
rather than reading undocumented remote PEB layouts.
